title: Israeli defense minister puts NATO power on notice as Middle East tensions surge: ‘Dangerous adventures’
summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz warned Recep Tayyip Erdoğan not to test Israel's resolve after the Abu al-Duhur airbase strike in Syria.
story: Amidst the NATO summit, President Donald Trump asserts the U.S. relationship with Turkey is 'better than it's ever been' despite F-35 concerns. However, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warns Turkey supports Hamas. Wall Street Journal's Olivia Beavers details Republican discomfort with Trump's stance, noting backchannel pushback against potentially shifting the Middle East's balance of power.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz issued a stark warning to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan early Thursday, accusing him of dragging Turkey into "dangerous adventures in Syria" and warning the Turkish leader not to test Israel’s resolve.

"Israel will not allow any actor to threaten its security," Katz wrote on X. "It would be better for Erdoğan to continue his detached-from-reality, fanciful rhetoric against Israel in the Turkish Grand National Assembly than to attempt to test Israel's determination to defend itself."

The warning comes two days after Israel struck Syria’s Abu al-Duhur Airbase. The increasingly heated rhetoric has put Washington in the position of trying to contain tensions between Turkey, a NATO member, and Israel, Washington’s closest security partners in the Middle East. Israel said Syria was on the verge of breaching a security understanding by allowing Turkish troops to deploy there, while Ankara rejected Israel’s account.

Syria said there were no plans for a permanent Turkish base or troop deployment, although Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani acknowledged that Turkish military officers had visited the facility for training and exchanges of expertise. Turkey’s Defense Ministry said no Turkish military delegation was present at the base before or during the strike, Reuters reported.
CRITICS SAY TURKEY'S VERBAL ATTACKS ON ISRAEL HAVE CROSSED INTO ANTISEMITISM
A satellite image shows craters on the runways of Abu al-Duhur Airbase near Syria's Aleppo after an Israeli attack, August 19, 2026. (Pleiades Neo © Airbus DS 2026/Handout via Reuters)

On Wednesday, Turkey called these allegations from Israel "untenable," arguing that they are "intended to legitimize Israel’s unlawful airstrikes targeting Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. ... The imputations voiced stem from Netanyahu’s intent to pursue expansionist and destabilizing policies in the region ahead of the elections in Israel," Turkey's government said in a social media post.

U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee told Reuters Thursday that Washington was working on "a de-escalation process" that was already in place but still needed to be refined. Asked whether the dispute could lead to a direct Israeli-Turkish confrontation, Huckabee said, "I don't think we're even close to that." He said Israel viewed Turkey as "moving further south" in Syria and perceived that as potentially threatening.

U.S. Ambassador to Turkey and special envoy for Syria Tom Barrack sounded a sharper warning after the strike. Barrack said Turkey had received no advance notice and could have prepared a military response after detecting Israeli aircraft heading north toward Turkish territory. He said Washington was working to establish a more robust deconfliction mechanism among Turkey, Israel and Syria to prevent miscalculation or an accidental confrontation.
Sinan Ciddi, director of the Turkey Program at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital that Ankara is portraying the confrontation through a sharply different lens.
FORMER SYRIAN PRESIDENT ASSAD SENTENCED TO DEATH IN ABSENTIA
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and Defense Minister Israel Katz attend a meeting. (GPO)

"Turkey is chalking up the increasingly escalatory climate between Turkey and Israel to election antics/propaganda by Netanyahu and driving a narrative that Israel does not want stable neighbors and regional powers in the Middle East," Ciddi said.

At the same time, Ciddi said Erdoğan "seems intent on taking actions inside Syria that are perceived by Israel as military escalation," citing proposed arms sales, military training and assistance, continued Turkish influence over former militia members integrated into Syria’s new army and, most significantly, "developing military bases with Turkish troops and sensitive equipment."
"Israel established clear red lines about what it was willing to tolerate in Syria," Ciddi said. "Deconfliction only works if parties implement the agreed upon rules."
NETANYAHU WARNS TURKEY SHOULD NOT GET F-35S, CITING ERDOĞAN'S HOSTILITY TOWARD NATO ALLIES
Syria's president Ahmed al-Sharaa and Turkey's President Tayyip Erdoğan attend a joint press conference at the Presidential Palace in Ankara, Turkey, February 4, 2025. (Cagla Gurdogan/Reuters)

The dispute was already being discussed at senior levels before the strike. Mossad chief Roman Gofman spoke with al-Shaibani on Aug. 14, four days before the attack, according to three sources cited by Reuters. The conversation focused on Israel’s concerns about Turkey’s military presence in Syria, including potential troop deployments, weapons sales and drones supplied to the Syrian military.

Attempts to prevent an Israeli-Turkish clash are not new. Turkey and Israel began technical talks in Azerbaijan in 2025 aimed at preventing misunderstandings or military incidents in Syria. Turkey’s defense minister said in June 2025 that those contacts were continuing as Ankara trained and advised Syria’s military.
Ciddi argued that a mechanism alone would not prevent further Israeli action if Ankara continued pushing against what Jerusalem considers its security red lines.
TRUMP'S TURKEY ARMS SALE PROPOSAL SPARKS CONGRESSIONAL QUESTIONS BEFORE NATO SUMMIT

Decommissioned Syrian air force planes are seen at the Abu Duhur military airbase east of Idlib, following the takeover of the area by Syrian opposition fighters on Dec. 7, 2024. (AP Photo/Omar Albam, File)

"To the extent that Ankara will push boundaries and attempt to position military capabilities that Israel feels is harmful to its safety, we are likely to see pre-emptive action by Jerusalem," Ciddi said. "The ball is in Erdoğan's court to not raise the temperature."

Netanyahu is also facing criticism from inside Israel. Former Prime Minister Ehud Barak, a longtime Netanyahu adversary, accused the prime minister Wednesday of deliberately escalating tensions with Turkey for political purposes ahead of the Israeli election.

"Turkey is not Iran or Assad’s Syria," Barak wrote in Hebrew on X, arguing that Israel’s strategic disputes with Ankara could be resolved, moderated or postponed through discreet diplomacy coordinated with the United States.

Turkish President Tayyip Erdoğan speaks during a rally in solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza, amid the ongoing conflict between Israel and the Palestinian Islamist group Hamas, in Istanbul, Turkey October 28, 2023. (Dilara Senkaya/Reuters)

title: Melting Swiss glacier reveals remains of two Belgian mountaineers missing since 1992
summary: DNA testing confirmed remains found on a Swiss Alps glacier belong to two Belgian mountaineers who vanished in the Weissmies region in 1992.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A melting glacier in the Swiss Alps revealed the remains of two Belgian mountaineers who vanished more than three decades ago, authorities said Wednesday.
A hiker spotted the remains on the Trift Glacier on July 26 after melting ice exposed them, according to police in Switzerland’s Valais canton.
Authorities recovered the remains and sent them to a forensic medicine institute at a hospital in Sion for identification.
REMAINS FOUND IN UTAH DESERT 28 YEARS AGO WITH HELP OF A PSYCHIC FINALLY IDENTIFIED THROUGH DNA GENEALOGY
A view of the Trift suspension bridge at the Trift Glacier in Valais, Switzerland, on Jan. 2, 2018. (BlueRed/REDA/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)
DNA testing showed they belonged to two Belgian men who disappeared in the Weissmies region in 1992, police said. The men were 39 and 41 when they went missing.
Valais police have kept records of missing-person cases dating to 1925. Many involve people who disappeared in the mountains or in bodies of water.
The glacial ice avalanche of the Trift Glacier above the village in Saas-Grund, Valais, Switzerland, Sunday, Sept. 10, 2017. (Dominic Steinmann/Keystone via AP, File)
WOMAN FOUND IN SHALLOW GRAVE ID’D AFTER 44 YEARS AS MILLIONAIRE TIED TO ESTATE MURDER PLOT
As glaciers retreat, remains hidden beneath the ice for decades can emerge, police said.
Similar discoveries have been made in Switzerland in recent years. In 2023, DNA testing identified a body found on a glacier near the Matterhorn as a German mountaineer who disappeared in 1986.
Regional police shared an image of Trift Glacier near Saas-Grund, Valais, Switzerland. (Valais Cantonal Police)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Switzerland’s glaciers have been melting at an increasing rate, a trend some scientists have linked to rising global temperatures.

title: Christian Zionists take on anti-Israel ‘propaganda’ from biblical heartland
summary: The Israel Guys inaugurated a major visitor center in Har Bracha on the West Bank, inviting Christians in Israel to see Judea and Samaria's biblical heartland firsthand.
story: CEO of The Israel Guys Joshua Waller urges Christians to ignore the propaganda and see Israel for themselves as his group opens a new visitor center in the biblical heartland.

A major visitors center in the West Bank town of Har Bracha in Samaria was inaugurated last month by The Israel Guys, a Christian Zionist organization that has spent nearly two decades bringing more than 5,000 volunteers from 35 countries to help develop the Land of Israel.

Joshua Waller, CEO of The Israel Guys, originally established as HaYovel, said the organization’s mission is to bring people to see for themselves how the biblical heartland is flourishing, despite what he says are media narratives portraying the area as beset by conflict.

"We live here, we see the people who live here, and then we tell everyone what is actually happening. Our role is to expand that and bring thousands of internationals to come and see for themselves," he told Fox News Digital.
US AMBASSADOR HUCKABEE SLAMS EXTREME GROUP OF ISRAELI SETTLERS FOR SEIZING PALESTINIAN HOMES ON WEST BANK
Joshua Waller of the Israel Guys at work on the West Bank. (The Israel Guys)

"You may love the Jewish people but be unsure how to deal with the propaganda, specifically the term ‘settler violence.’ Jews in Judea and Samaria have been branded as a radical group that would probably be dangerous to encounter. Well, come to the visitor center, and you will see the exact opposite," he said.
"You will see that it is a fake narrative built by the international community … it is a straight-up war against the Jewish [people]," he added.

The organization’s volunteer programs include the Heartland Experience, a 10-day trip to Israel combining touring, volunteer work and interaction with local residents; the Grape Harvest trip, a two-week program held in late summer and early fall that focuses on helping farmers with the harvest; and the Men’s Pruning trip, a two-week program in early spring focused on pruning vineyards.
Other programs include Zion Ops, a four-week program for young adults ages 18 to 30, and Day Visits, which offer two-hour visits to Har Bracha.
ISRAEL LAUNCHES 'BIBLICAL HIGHWAY' AMID CAMPAIGN TO ERASE JEWISH HISTORY
Volunteers working in vineyards on the West Bank are part of the Israel Guys' program that brings volunteers to Israel. (The Israel Guys)

In 2004, Tommy Waller, Joshua Waller’s father, traveled to Israel for the first time, where he met Nir Lavi, founder of Har Bracha Winery. Lavi shared his plan to fulfill the vision of the Prophet Jeremiah: "You shall again plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria; the planters shall plant and eat them as ordinary food" (Jeremiah 31:5).
Waller Sr. asked how he could help.

In 2007, after moving with his wife, Sherri, and their 11 children from Tennessee to Har Bracha, Waller Sr. established HaYovel, a U.S. nonprofit that provides Christian volunteers with an opportunity to work the land alongside Israeli farmers.

In 2013, the organization sought to counter anti-Israel rhetoric by launching The Joshua & Caleb Report TV show, its first dedicated pro-Israel media project, which in 2018 transitioned into a weekly podcast. Five years ago, the organization rebranded as The Israel Guys and stepped up its advocacy efforts.
CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM
"HaYovel" volunteers from its international program work in the vineyards of Shiloh in Samaria help to pick grapes on the West Bank. (Hillel Maeir/TPS-IL)

The Israel Guys currently counts more than 20 team members and, since its founding, has helped develop some 120 farms. Volunteers who come to Judea and Samaria work alongside local farmers, planting trees, erecting fences, harvesting crops and assisting with infrastructure projects.

In the aftermath of the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, massacre of 1,200 Israelis, The Israel Guys launched Operation Ittai and raised $3.85 million to provide tactical supplies to communities in the area and strengthen their defenses against possible terrorist attacks.
Anti-Israel activists protest outside the United Nations headquarters in New York on April 7, 2025. (Selcuk Acar/Anadolu via Getty Images)
The group went viral at the time after bringing American cowboys to Israel to help farmers whose workers had been called up as reservists.
Addressing media coverage of recent incidents involving Christians in Israel, Waller said the narrative that they are no longer welcome in the country is false.
AMBASSADOR GEORGE DEEK: THE CHRISTIAN ISRAEL YOU ARE NOT BEING SHOWN
Josh Waller works the field in the West Bank, also known by its biblical names Judea and Samaria. (The Israel Guys)

"People put a lot of money into trying to make it seem as though Christians would somehow be better off living in Iran, Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, Jordan or other Arab countries surrounding Israel. Factually, that is completely wrong," he told Fox News Digital.

"I know Christians living in those places, and I even know Christians living in areas under the control of the Palestinian Authority, and they suffer immensely. The fact is that Israel is the safest place for Christians in the entire Middle East. It is the only place where the Christian population is growing," he added.
Volunteers, Waller explained, have come from a wide range of Christian denominations, including Catholics, Protestants, Evangelicals, Mormons, Amish and Mennonites.
The new center will include programs to support Israeli farmers, lectures on Israel and Zionism and be a place for communal meals. (The Israel Guys)
He emphasized that Israel is a partner for peace and urged nations to align themselves with biblical values, which he said could pave the way for "some incredible days ahead."

If antisemitism leads to efforts to destroy Israel, he added, "that’s not an option," saying Israel would have to fight that war while The Israel Guys would continue to "help on the information side."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"The Bible says that this land that was desolate will become like the Garden of Eden. We are literally seeing it happen. It’s beautiful to see volunteers participate in the fulfillment of that prophecy and witness the ancient words of the Bible come back to life," Waller said.
Amelie Botbol is a freelance field reporter based in Tel Aviv, Israel, who reports on Israel-related news.

title: Military trial date set for alleged mastermind of Sept. 11 attacks
summary: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, who has been held at Guantánamo Bay since 2006, is scheduled to go on trial in June 2028.
story: A military judge ruled Wednesday that the man accused of being the mastermind behind the 9/11 attacks will stand trial starting in June 2028.
Khalid Sheikh Mohammed will be prosecuted alongside others suspected of conspiring in the attacks: Walid bin Attash, Ali Abdul Aziz Ali and Mustafa Ahmed al-Hawsawi.

Mohammed is accused of orchestrating the plot to crash hijacked planes into the World Trade Center in New York and the Pentagon on Sept. 11, 2001. A third plane was crashed in a field in Pennsylvania during the attacks.
He has been held at the U.S. naval base at Guantánamo Bay, Cuba, since 2006.
Air Force Lt. Col. Michael Schrama, a military commissions judge, on Wednesday rejected the January 2027 start date proposed by prosecutors and instead set the trial date for about 18 months later.

The trial date was announced after a split federal appeals court last summer threw out a potential agreement that would have allowed Mohammed to plead guilty in exchange for sparing him the risk of execution.
Mohammed was charged and arraigned in 2008 with war crimes and murder in connection with the nearly 3,000 people who died in the 9/11 attacks.

The road to prosecute Mohammed and other conspirators has dragged on for years, with the Obama-era military commissions system being tested for the first time — at times leading to lengthy challenges to its rules.

Defense lawyers have also argued that the holdup comes from what they say are the government’s efforts to hide details of torture used against detainees at secret CIA prisons before they were transferred to Guantánamo Bay.
Mohammed was captured in Pakistan in 2003 before being transferred to Guantánamo Bay three years later.

A Senate report from 2014 found that the CIA had used what it called “enhanced interrogation techniques” against Mohammed and other conspirators, including waterboarding Mohammed 183 times in what was described as “a series of near-drownings.”

title: Panda Express’ CEOs are on a ‘mission’ to help workers achieve the dream of home ownership
summary: Panda Express founders Andrew and Peggy Cherng want to be known for helping their workers build careers and eventually buy their own homes.
story: Panda Express is famous for its orange chicken. But the founders of the iconic fast-casual Asian chain also want to be known for something else: helping their workers realize the American dream.

“I always believe that when you do well, you know, personally, then you can go out and take care of other people,” said Andrew Cherng, who is co-founder, co-chair and co-CEO of Panda Express along with his wife, Peggy Cherng.
“You want people to do well,” he said. “And you want to treat them well.”

Cherng measures progress in part by how many of his managers make $100,000 or more annually. He also tracks whether those managers can afford to buy homes, and he considers that a barometer of his own success.
Yet over the past decade, that American dream of homeownership has slipped out of reach for millions of middle-class families.
With low housing stock across the country, mortgage rates hovering at 6.8% and home prices in some cities at record levels, there is little relief in sight.

Immigrant families are also less likely to own their homes than families headed by native-born U.S. residents, according to census data. Experts point to several factors that are likely to contribute to the disparity, including limited employment and income prospects, language barriers and inconsistent access to banks and financing.
Peggy Cherng said the couple recognize elements of their own journeys in those of their employees. “Most of our associates are first-generation immigrants,” she said.
Andrew was born in China and immigrated to the U.S. in 1966 after having grown up in Taiwan and Japan. Peggy was born in Myanmar and raised in Hong Kong.

The couple met at the University of Missouri and opened their first Panda Express in 1983 in Glendale, California. At the time, they envisioned it as a casual offshoot of Panda Inn, the full-service Chinese restaurant Andrew opened with his father in the early 1970s.
That immigrant experience remains central to how the couple run the business today, particularly a focus on investing in their employees, whom they consider their extended family.

Today, Panda Express is America’s largest Asian restaurant chain, with more than 2,500 locations across 49 states and restaurants in 12 countries. The privately held company employs around 55,000 people and generates around $7 billion in annual sales, according to data compiled by market research firm Technomic.
For Andrew, the foundation of that success is built from the ground up — starting with his employees.
“How do we help these people to have a better life? That’s our mission,” he said in an interview at the company’s headquarters outside Los Angeles, part of NBC News’ “Business in America” initiative.

Peggy said, “Our mission, our calling, is how we are able to help more associates realize their American dream, establish their business, their career, but most importantly, mark that accomplishment by owning a home.”
And despite the long list of obstacles to first-time homeownership, Andrew wants to help his Panda Express employees focus on what is possible rather than what stands in their way.
“We actually help everybody to think about owning a home very quickly,” he said.
Many of the managers he hires initially seem to view the position as just another job, he said, not a potential career path.
Managers “have to do a lot of things,” he said. “We teach them [those skills], but to have a good life, you turn that person from being sort of ‘task-based’ to ‘life-based.’”
That transformation, according to Andrew, often instills a deeper sense of purpose in his employees — one that extends to caring for others and their communities.
“We get people to see that quickly and see it clearly,” he said.

title: A near-total lunar eclipse will be visible across the U.S. Thursday night
summary: Two weeks after a total solar eclipse wowed skywatchers in Europe, a near-total lunar eclipse is in store Thursday for people in North and South America.
story: Two weeks after a total solar eclipse wowed skywatchers in southern Europe, a near-total lunar eclipse is set to put on a show Thursday night for people across North and South America.

Lunar eclipses occur when Earth slips between the sun and the moon and casts a shadow on the lunar surface. During this week’s event, nearly the entire moon — 96.2% at the eclipse’s peak — will be shrouded in Earth’s shadow.
Weather permitting, skywatchers in the continental U.S. will have some of the best views. The eclipse will also be visible elsewhere in North America, South America, parts of Europe and Africa.

During the eclipse, Earth’s shadow will appear reddish orange on the lunar surface because of the way Earth’s atmosphere scatters light from the sun. That’s why a total lunar eclipse is also known as a “blood moon.”

Thursday’s eclipse will begin at 9:23 p.m. ET, when the moon first enters the outer part of Earth’s shadow. The real action gets underway, however, at 10:33 p.m. ET, when Earth’s shadow starts to envelop the lunar surface, appearing to take a “bite” out of the lunar disk.
The eclipse will peak at 12:12 a.m. ET, when more than 96% of the lunar surface will be shrouded. The event will end at 3:01 a.m. ET when the moon exits the outer edge of Earth’s shadow.

Most viewers in North and South America, except those in Alaska and the northernmost reaches of Canada, will have a chance to see every stage of the lunar eclipse. For those in Europe and Africa, however, the eclipse will begin early Friday, and the moon will set as the event is progressing.
Unlike solar eclipses, lunar eclipses can be viewed safely with the naked eye, and skywatchers can use binoculars and telescopes to catch more dramatic views.

The lunar eclipse follows a total solar eclipse — when the sun, the moon and Earth align, with the moon passing in front of the sun and blocking its light — that darkened skies in Spain, a small part of Portugal, Greenland, Iceland and northern Russia.

Solar and lunar eclipses usually come in pairs because of the fortuitous way the moon, Earth and sun interact. The three celestial bodies happen to align from our perspective on Earth because the sun is 400 times farther from Earth than the moon, while also being 400 times bigger. That makes them appear the same size in the sky.
Solar eclipses occur during the new moon phase. Typically around two weeks later, when the moon is on the other side of Earth from the sun, lunar eclipses occur during the full moon phase.

The next solar eclipse, on Feb. 6, will be visible in parts of South America and Africa. The next lunar eclipse will occur overnight from Feb. 20 to 21. It should be visible in North and South America, Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia and Antarctica, according to NASA.

title: PGA Tour CEO blasts ‘concerning’ Good Good Golf ad that depicted co-founder shoving female golfer onto the ground
summary: Good Good Golf took down the ad, saying it “depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand.” PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp called the brand’s response “disappointing.”
story: Good Good Golf is facing the wrath of the golf industry after it posted a controversial ad that depicted one of its co-founders shoving a female golfer to the ground.

The commercial, which promoted Good Good Golf and Callaway Golf’s Quantum Driver collaboration and has since been taken down, sparked outrage online, with viewers saying it appeared to promote domestic violence and violence against women.
PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp condemned the commercial Tuesday, calling it “concerning” and “clearly not aligned with PGA Tour values.”

The commercial showed golfer Alexis Miestowski trying to grab a driver out of a golf bag, only to be shoved to the ground by Good Good Golf co-founder Garrett Clark. After having pushed her, he stands over her and warns: “Do not touch my new driver.”
Good Good Golf said in a statement Saturday that the ad “ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand.”
“We have since taken that content down, and sincerely apologize,” it said.
The public, however, wasn’t pacified by the apology. Neither were some sponsors.

An X user responded to Good Good Golf’s statement, “Why would a company take the time to shoot, produce, and then put out a video on all their social channels that isn’t aligned with their values as a brand?”

Good Good Golf started out as a YouTube channel and grew into an independent media and apparel company. The premiere Tuesday night of its Golf Channel reality show, “Big Break X Good Good,” was postponed because one of the sponsors wanted to drop out following the ad fallout.
PGA Tour leadership didn’t buy the apology statement, either.
Rolapp told reporters Tuesday that Good Good Golf’s initial response was “disappointing” and “a bit defensive and late.”
“But I think the responses are getting better. I think we’ve seen some things this morning; we had some conversations with them,” Rolapp continued. “But no, we were disappointed with what we saw.”
He said the PGA Tour will continue to “monitor” and work with Good Good Golf. It comes at a critical time as Good Good Golf is the title sponsor of a new PGA Tour event in Austin, Texas, this fall.
Callaway Golf CEO Chip Brewer also apologized for the ad Saturday, saying, “While the video was produced by Good Good, it was approved by Callaway prior to voting.”
“That approval should never have happened. Mistakes were made, and we are taking the matter very seriously,” he continued.

Brewer apologized for the video, saying, “To be clear: we are unequivocally against discrimination, domestic violence, or threatening behavior of any kind.” He said the company is also conducting internal and external investigations and has changed its approval processes to ensure “this will never happen again.”
While Good Good Golf and Callaway are mired in the controversy, another brand is turning it into its marketing punch line.
Parsons Xtreme Golf shared an ad Tuesday showing various women golfing, with the caption: “Our drivers play nice with everyone. #SheGolfs.”

title: Serena and Venus Williams set to play doubles together at U.S. Open
summary: Serena and Venus Williams received a wild card to play doubles together at the U.S. Open next week, the United States Tennis Association announced.
story: QUEENS, N.Y. — Four years after a pseudo-retirement, Serena Williams is back in the U.S. Open for a shot at redemption. And this time, she’s teaming up with her older sister Venus.
The Williams sisters received a wild card Wednesday and will play doubles together next week, the United States Tennis Association announced.

This will mark the 10th time the pair have played alongside one another in the U.S. Open, a doubles event they have won twice in 1999 and 2009, respectively. The duo has captured 14 major titles together.

The news of their return comes less than a day after Serena Williams, 44, teamed up with 23-year-old phenom Carlos Alcaraz in a dramatic mixed doubles run Tuesday. Both returning from injury, Williams and Alcaraz — who boasts seven Grand Slam singles titles — wooed fans with dazzling rallies and impassioned gameplay in an opening round win before getting knocked out in the quarterfinals by Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.
Following the loss, Williams told NBC News she was just happy to be back on the court.

“It felt great,” she said. “I haven’t played a ton of tennis, but it still felt good to kind of get back out there and just kind of feel your groove. I honestly never, ever thought I would be back here playing tennis. So it’s kind of surreal.”

Williams is widely considered the greatest women’s tennis player of all time. She has 39 Grand Slam titles (23 singles, 14 women’s doubles and two mixed doubles) and spent 319 weeks ranked No. 1 in the world. Along with Steffi Graf, she is one of only two women to win all four Grand Slam singles titles and an Olympic singles gold medal.
Though she never officially retired, she said she was “evolving away from tennis” in 2022.
Alcaraz, the world No. 3 player, called it a “privilege” to play alongside Williams this week at the U.S. Open.
“I felt the pressure,” he said. “It’s kind of as if I was playing the final of the Grand Slam. I just loved it and I enjoyed every single second.”
Alcarez is coming off a four-month layoff following a right wrist injury he suffered at the Barcelona Open in April.

Williams, meanwhile, returned in June to competitive tennis after a four-year break only to injure her right knee during her first-round singles match at Wimbledon. Given the time away from the game and additional recovery, she noted that her relationship with the game has evolved.

“My relationship with tennis is like a love hate thing,” she told NBC News. “I love it, and then I hate to lose … But it’s definitely more fun now. I just try my best not to put as much pressure on myself.”
The first round of the women’s doubles tournament begins Sept. 3.

title: Infant in Pennsylvania is one of two people reported to die of measles this week
summary: The deaths were the first associated with measles in the state in 35 years.
story: One of the two people who recently died of measles in Pennsylvania was an infant, the state Health Department said Wednesday.
The department announced Tuesday that two unvaccinated residents had died of measles, the first measles-related deaths in the U.S. this year and the first in Pennsylvania in 35 years.

On Wednesday, the department said one of those deaths was under investigation by the Lancaster County Coroner’s Office, which had said it was reviewing the death of an infant with a positive measles test.
The Health Department did not specify the ages of either person who died.
Both were residents of Lancaster County, where the share of kids who have gotten the MMR vaccine fell from 95.5% in 2017 to 87.6% last year.
The Health Department has confirmed 424 measles cases this year, 94 of them diagnosed in the past week. So far, 73 people have been hospitalized for measles complications.
The first dose of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine is recommended at 12 to 15 months and the second at 4 to 6 years.

“The real vulnerability is in infants between 6 and 11 months of age, as maternal antibody is waning and they haven’t gotten their first dose of the MMR vaccine,” said Dr. Peter Hotez, dean of the National School of Tropical Medicine at Baylor College of Medicine in Dallas.

In places where infants have a high risk of measles exposure, health authorities sometimes recommend an early dose of the vaccine for babies starting at 6 months old. That was the case during an outbreak in Texas last year, when two unvaccinated girls died of the disease.
Nationwide, 2,777 measles cases have been confirmed this year, the most in 35 years.

Measles has been considered eliminated in the U.S. since 2000 because it has not continuously spread over a yearlong period. The Pan American Health Organization is expected to decide in November whether the U.S. has lost its elimination status.

title: Trump flexes as the Freedom Caucus fades: From the Politics Desk
summary: In today’s edition, we break down the key takeaways from the latest round of primaries.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
In today’s edition, we break down the key takeaways from the latest round of primaries. Plus, Andrea Mitchell looks at the aftermath of the Abbey Gate attack five years later.
Sign up to receive this newsletter in your inbox every weekday here.
— Adam Wollner
Trump flexes as the Freedom Caucus fades: 3 primary night lessons

Tuesday marked the final multistate primary day of the year. After a few more nominating contests in New England next month, we will be firmly in general election mode.But before we get there, let’s review three lessons we learned from the primary runoffs in South Carolina and Oklahoma.

Trump’s endorsement is still potent: It had been an unusually tough month for Republicans backed by President Donald Trump. Of the nine candidates he endorsed in House, Senate and gubernatorial primaries who have suffered defeats this year, six came in August.

But Trump bounced back in a big way last night, pushing appointed Sen. Darline Graham — whom he had recruited to run for the seat held by her late brother — across the finish line in South Carolina. Trump went beyond his usual level of support for primary candidates — supportive Truth Social posts and tele-rallies — and held an in-person event with Graham days out from Election Day. It seems to have paid dividends: Graham won Horry County, where the rally took place, by nearly 47 points over Rep. Ralph Norman.
Trump also eked out a win in Oklahoma. His endorsed candidate, former state Sen. Mike Mazzei, defeated Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond in the primary runoff for governor by 2,000 votes.
And so is his money: Trump went to bat for Graham in another key way. His allied super PAC, MAGA Inc., poured $830,000 into phone calls and text messages to voters ahead of the runoff.

MAGA Inc., which had more than $400 million on hand at the end of July, has otherwise been hesitant to open up its coffers this election season. The last time the group shelled out money for a Republican candidate came during a special House election in Georgia in March, when it spent $18,000.
Graham’s success may further fuel calls from Republicans for MAGA Inc. to spread the wealth as the party confronts a difficult political environment this fall.

The Freedom Caucus’ ranks continue to thin: Norman’s loss to Graham also marked a defeat for the hard-right House Freedom Caucus, as Sahil Kapur notes. (The congressman had also finished in third place in South Carolina’s June primary for governor.)
Earlier this month, Rep. Andy Ogles, R-Tenn., a Freedom Caucus member who was backed by Trump, lost renomination. And in May, Rep. Chip Roy, R-Texas, lost the primary for state attorney general.

Freedom Caucus members have also won Senate or gubernatorial nominations this year in Alabama, Arizona, Florida and Wisconsin. But that also means, win or lose, none of them will be back in Congress next year, potentially limiting the group’s influence on Capitol Hill.

5 years after Abbey Gate

It has been five years since 13 American service members died at Abby Gate outside the Kabul airport in Afghanistan, killed by a suicide bombing as the troops were trying to help thousands of people desperate to escape before the Taliban takeover.

After a review of the risks the troops knowingly undertook, today the Pentagon elevated the posthumous valor awards for seven of the 11 Marines who died that day, having found that their commendations had been “inappropriately downgraded,” according to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth.

One hopes the belated honors provide some measure of comfort to the grieving families and friends of the fallen. But five years after the Taliban reasserted its rule, the world community is for the most part ignoring the humanitarian crisis for the people of Afghanistan. The same goes for the plight of Afghan refugees still stranded around the world, as well as Afghan veterans in the U.S. who worked with the country’s military during the war and are now under threat of being sent back to unsafe conditions.

The International Rescue Committee says its relief workers in Afghanistan have provided essential services to 15 million people since 2022, but what had been 46 health facilities at its peak is down to just 16 today. The sharp decline has occurred largely since the U.S. and other governments cut funding in 2025. According to the IRC, which has worked in Afghanistan for 40 years, its 2026 humanitarian appeal is only a quarter funded. The nongovernment agency cites nutrition and maternal health, as well as outreach to malnourished children and pregnant women in the provinces, as the greatest need.

With Sunday marking five years since the disastrous U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan, the IRC program director in Afghanistan, Bostan Fahim, appealed for help, saying, “At the exact moment Afghanistan’s hunger crisis hit its worst point in recorded history, the world pulled back the funding needed to respond.”

And despite bipartisan support for Afghan veterans in the U.S., they are now in legal jeopardy. The State Department has severely limited a refugee program that at its height accepted 120,000 people a year from all countries during the Biden administration. This year, the Trump administration has cut the total to 17,000 refugees a year, 12,000 of whom must be White Afrikaners, claiming without evidence they as a group are targeted for racial discrimination.

New bipartisan legislation introduced in Congress would provide Temporary Protected Status to Afghans in the U.S. who cannot safely return home because of their work during the war. U.S. veterans’ groups strongly support the effort. But their cause lost ground with the administration when an Afghan veteran last year was accused of shooting two National Guard service members near the White House, killing one and severely injuring the other. It became a rallying cry for the administration’s opposition to permitting other refugees to remain.

For five years, the U.S. has investigated and debated the calamity of the Afghan withdrawal. Images of the multitudes desperately trying to board the last flights out of Kabul are seared in our memories. Women in Afghanistan are once again being denied education, jobs and independent identities, along with the overriding absence of adequate healthcare, proper nutrition and clean water. International aid groups say it is long past time to remember the needs of those left behind who are living with the consequences of decades of war, repression and abandonment.

title: How to clean your dishwasher in 5 simple steps, according to a cleaning expert
summary: If you’ve ever thought about how to clean a dishwasher, this is the best way to do it. I talked to cleaning experts for their guidance and product recommendations.
story: We don’t always have the answers, but we have some people on speed dial who do — which is why we present to you our series FYI where we have experts explain if hair removal cream is actually bad, how often you should change your towels and more.

You probably clean your kitchen counters, stovetop and floors regularly — but you might not be able to say the same for your dishwasher. Dishwashers are great at clearing away remnants of dinners past from your dishes, but they may not be as clean as they appear.

The dishwasher’s filter is a hotbed for food residue and soap scum, according to Kadi Dulude, owner of cleaning company Wizards of Homes. “When not removed in time, [debris] will clog the filter, food particles will start smelling bad and the machine won’t operate properly because it’s not draining anymore,” she says. The good news is cleaning a dishwasher doesn’t require expensive tools or special skills — just a little guidance.
We consulted cleaning experts for their insight about the best way to clean a dishwasher, and for their recommendations of products to use to do it

The brushes are also dishwasher safe, so you can add them with a load of dishes after each use.
What is the best way to clean a dishwasher?

The best way to deep clean a dishwasher involves hand washing the different components of the machine, including the racks, filter and spray arms. I spoke with Ryan Knoll, the owner of cleaning company TidyCasa, for the best step-by-step way to clean a dishwasher. Here’s what he recommends:

Remove the racks, spray arms and filter from the dishwasher. Use mild dish soap, a scrub brush and warm, soapy water to scrub them. If needed, use a toothbrush to scrub parts of the filter. Rinse the racks, spray arms and filter with water and set those aside.

Wipe away any debris from the bottom of the dishwasher. With mild dish soap and a scrub brush, scrub the interior of the dishwasher with warm soapy water. Add the racks, spray arms and filter back into the dishwasher.

Fill a dishwasher-safe measuring cup with one cup of distilled white vinegar and place it on the top rack of the dishwasher, making sure it’s sitting upright. Close the dishwasher and run it on the hottest cycle. Remove the vinegar after the cycle is complete and then run the dishwasher again.

As an alternative to step three, use a dishwasher cleaner. Follow the instructions on the label. If you use the Finish Dishwasher Deep Cleaner or Glisten Dishwasher Cleaner, remove the top of the container, place the bottle upside down on the bottom rack or wherever it says in the directions and run the dishwasher on the hot water cycle. If you’re using a dishwasher cleaning tablet, then simply place it in the compartment before running the appliance.

If it’s a stainless steel dishwasher, use a stainless steel cleaning spray and microfiber cloth or stainless steel cleaning wipe to clean the outside of the dishwasher door. Otherwise, use mild dish soap and a damp microfiber cloth to wipe the outside. Wipe away the residue with a dry microfiber cloth.
How we picked the best products for cleaning a dishwasher

Your dishwasher may appear clean on the outside, but many of its parts — such as the filter and spray arms — collect debris and minerals over time. Our experts recommend keeping the following tips in mind when looking for products to clean a dishwasher:

Find specialized detergent: Dulude recommends against filling the detergent compartment of the dishwasher with regular liquid dish soap in general because it produces too much foam and suds. Instead use dishwasher detergents and/or tablets from brands like Finish, Affresh, Cascade and Glisten. These cleaners get rid of soap scum, food debris and limescale (residual minerals leftover from hard water), all of which are common causes of a smelly dishwasher. In fact, hard water residue buildup can decrease water pressure and affect the function of appliances, according to the United States Geological Survey. Go with acidic cleaning agents: You should also use acidic ingredients like distilled white vinegar to clean the inside of your dishwasher and its parts. That’s because the acidic nature of vinegar helps to lift and remove the stuck-on debris. Look for abrasive cleaning products: Abrasive ingredients and products, such as baking soda or a scrubbing brush, are ideal for cleaning parts of your dishwasher because they lift grime. Use a scratch-free sponge, dish brush or a Scrub Daddy.

How to keep a dishwasher clean

Once your dishwasher is clean, it’s important to maintain that cleanliness. Incorporating the simple steps below into your kitchen routine can help you stretch out the time between cleanings, which also saves you money on cleaners or ingredients in the long run.

Pre-rinse dishes: Even though some brands may say that rinsing dishes before putting them in the dishwasher isn’t necessary to get them clean, it’s still a good idea to rinse them to prevent small particles of food from getting stuck in the filter. This also helps prevent rotting food smells from forming in your appliance.Unload dishes immediately: You should remove the dishes from the machine as soon as the cycle finishes. That’s because, even though the dishes are technically clean, they can develop water stains. Using a rinse aid can also prevent this. Use a rinse aid: Speaking of rinse aids, picks like Finish Jet-Dry Rinse Aid, help your dishes dry faster, which ultimately prevents  them from developing hard water stains.

Frequently asked questions

Limescale is the crusty mineral deposit left over from hard water. It commonly forms in areas like faucets, sink drains, bathtubs and shower heads. Over time, buildup of limescale can prevent pipes from draining properly.

Soap scum is a mix of residual detergent and minerals found in hard water, like calcium. It typically forms as a dusty white film in areas where water mixes with residual soap, including sink drains, bathtubs, shower curtains and grout.

title: ‘Monster isn’t enough’: Family mourns 8 killed, including 4 kids, in Montana shooting
summary: A man killed eight relatives, including his sister and four children at a family dinner in Montana, weeks after his parents asked him to move out, authorities said Wednesday.
story: A man killed eight relatives, including his sister and four children at a family dinner in Montana, weeks after his parents asked him to move out, authorities said Wednesday.
The attack unfolded early Sunday evening on White Star Circle just outside of Billings, at a home owned by victims Dana Smith, 73, and Barbara Smith, 72, officials said.
The homeowners were killed along with Megan Ireland-Ghekiere, 39, and her four children Owen Ireland, 13, Chloe Ireland, 7, Landon Ghekiere, 15, and Charlotte Ghekiere, 12, authorities said.
Evelyn Smith, 92 — whom interim Yellowstone County Sheriff Kent O’Donnell called the “family matriarch” — did not live at the home but was there Sunday for dinner when she was killed.
O’Donnell identified the shooter as 44-year-old Alan Michael Smith, saying he carried out a “very complex” attack.
Smith is the brother of victim Megan Ireland-Ghekier and thus an uncle to all four of the younger victims, Billings police said.
Dana and Barbara Smith were the killer’s parents and Evelyn Smith his grandmother, according to police.
Smith had once lived in that house and had been asked to move out we
eks earlier, Brad Ireland — Megan Ireland-Ghekiere’s ex-husband — told The Associated Press.
O’Donnell confirmed that Alan Smith had once lived at the house but wasn’t currently residing there when the violence unfolded Sunday.
“This is an ongoing criminal investigation with eight victims, making this very complex,” O’Donnell said.

The killings wiped out members from four generations, said Jennifer Mercer, a neighbor and family friend who set up an online fundraiser to help cover funeral costs and other expenses, and was authorized to release these details.

Smith arrived at the home at about 5:49 p.m. and 11 minutes later neighbors believed they heard the sound of fireworks, officials said. That kind of noise, especially in the summer, wouldn’t necessarily alarm anyone, O’Donnell said.
But at 6:02 p.m., dispatchers received a call from a “female” voice inside the house, and Yellowstone County sheriff’s deputies arrived at 6:10 p.m., officials said.
The children were all very close and everyone got along with their parents remaining amicable even after divorcing, according to Mercer.
“Charlotte was the hero that dialed 911,” Mercer said in statement to NBC News. “She tried to save her family. She lived by her favorite quote, ‘I love you more.’ ”
When police officers and deputies arrived, they were “confronted the suspect in the front yard, where he retreated into the house,” O’Donnell said.
More “gunshots were heard within the household” before the shooter went to the back of the property, O’Donnell said.
At about 6:13 p.m., a deputy “heard a final shot, which was broken away from the rest of the shots,” according to the sheriff.
By about 6:22, police officers and sheriff’s deputies “made entrance into the backyard” and located a male victim there with a gunshot wound beginning life-saving measures on him,  O’Donnell said.

“At this time, it wasn’t known that he was actually the suspect of all this,” O’Donnell said. “He was just a person down, and law enforcement did what they’re trained to do. They got him out of the hot zone and provided what first aid they could. He was pronounced dead upon arrival at the hospital.”
The blaze continued until about 1 a.m. Monday, according to Billings Fire Department Chief Matt Hoppel.
Another complicating factor in the fire was that the house sat outside Billings city limits on county land where fire hydrants were not mandatory.
“They had to haul in truckloads of water, set up a temporary tank and pump out of that tank,” O’Donnell said. “So the fire suppression portion of this was very very difficult.”
The Smith family came to Montana from the Seattle area.
When Megan Ghekiere and Ireland divorced six years ago, she moved to Montana with their children, the ex-husband said.
Megan Ghekiere would then meet Adam Ghekiere, who would become her second husband. He was working and not at the Smith home when gunfire erupted.
“We are so grateful for the prayers, the love, the support that we’re getting from the nation,” Ghekiere said.
The blended family appeared to be very close, emotionally and geographically with Evelyn Smith, Dana’s elderly mother, living in a nearby retirement home, according to Ireland,
“They were nice,” neighbor Donna Heisler, 67, told NBC News on Tuesday.  “I talked to Barbara the wife at a couple of garage sales.”
Heisler said her neighbors appeared to enjoy their privacy.
“They kind of kept to themselves. Really weren’t a very outgoing couple,” Heisler said. “They weren’t the socialites on the block so you’d see them once in a while but they weren’t overly outgoing.”
She added: “And coming from a bigger city maybe more the way they preferred to have it.”
Ireland said Alan Smith had moved in with his parents in Montana and stayed with them for years before being asked to leave a couple weeks ago.
Ireland called Alan Smith  a “hermit”  and “no one knew what he did in there 24/7.”
Smith’s name was not connected to any criminal records in Montana and Washington.

“We had not been called to this residence before, and we had not had any prior contact with the suspect,” O’Donnell said. “We had not been called to this residence before, and we had not had any prior contact with the suspect.”
Adam Ghekiere, who works at the airport in Billings, learned of the shootings over dispatch radio and when he couldn’t reach family of the phone he raced to the crime scene.
Ghekiere’s children weren’t supposed to be there, the grieving father said, because family dinner was usually on Friday.
Ghekiere said police have confirmed to him that his daughter, Charlotte, was the one who dialed 911 from inside the house.
“I keep hearing her — every time I would say ‘I love you,’ she would say ‘I love you more,’ ” Ghekiere told the wire service.

title: Mike Lindell won’t pay for recount in Minnesota GOP primary, sues election officials
summary: The MyPillow founder, a fierce Trump ally, said last week that he would pay $825,000 to fund a full hand recount after he lost the Republican gubernatorial primary.
story: MyPillow founder Mike Lindell, a longtime 2020 election denier, sued the Minnesota secretary of state and election officials, claiming they changed the scope of a potential recount in the GOP gubernatorial primary this month.

Lindell, who lost Aug. 11 to state House Speaker Lisa Demuth by about 45,000 votes, said last week that he would pay $825,000 on Monday to cover the cost of a full hand recount and audit of the race, in which he finished a distant second despite an endorsement from President Donald Trump.
The deadline for payment came and went without the money from Lindell.

He told NBC News in a phone call Tuesday that he refused to pay after he was informed that a recount would focus on the ballots cast for him or Demuth, rather than every ballot cast in the seven-candidate Republican field.

“I paid this to have all of the votes counted, not just two people,” he said. “I need to have a real recount, and I will fight this in court and get that real recount. I don’t care if it costs triple. I didn’t hold back anything. They did a bait-and-switch on me, and it’s disgusting.”
The secretary of state’s office said in a statement that it provided the contingent recount plan to Lindell after the State Canvassing Board approved it on Aug. 18.
The office said that “the plan follows state law and administrative rules on recount procedures and is consistent with previous recount plans.”
The lawsuits against the secretary of state’s office and the State Canvassing Board dispute the recount process the state outlined and seek to ensure no recount takes place based on those parameters.
Secretary of State Steve Simon, a Democrat, is chair of the canvassing board.

Lindell, who has repeated debunked claims that the 2020 election was rigged by voting machines, said last week that his team found several “irregularities” in the election data, arguing that they were due to the use of electronic voting machines.
Demuth is set to face Democratic nominee Amy Klobuchar in the general election.
Leading up to the Minnesota primary, Lindell has faced multiple lawsuits from voting machine companies after he claimed the 2020 presidential election was fraudulent.

In one of the defamation cases, Lindell now owes even more in court fees than he does in sanctions after he refused to pay Smartmatic USA Corp., a voting machine company. Lindell said last week that he still does not plan to pay what the court says he owes.
He also was found to have defamed a former employee of Dominion Voting Systems in June 2025.

title: Dolly Parton Had Many Projects In the Works Before Her Death. Where They Stand

story: Before her death, Dolly Parton had a slew of projects she was excited about bringing to life and sharing with her millions of fans.
On Aug. 26, a day after the country icon died at the age of 80, her team shared an update on all the plans she had in development.

“Dolly worked up until the day she died. She loved seeing her dreams come to life, and loved knowing her work brought people joy,” her longtime manager Danny Nozell said in a press release. “Ever the planner, Dolly worked with the team that she handpicked, for the past several years to build a project roadmap that will guide us for decades to come.”
Parton died after being diagnosed with cancer, her estate announced Aug. 25 in a statement. She had not publicly disclosed her diagnosis, but had been open about her ongoing health challenges.

While the beloved star’s death came as a shock to many, she prepared for her legacy to live on. Nozell said in his statement that he and Parton’s team will oversee the many projects she had been working on and “ensure the many dreams she had yet to fulfill are brought to life.”
He noted that many projects were in various stages of development, stressing that Parton approved everything that would be shared on her official channels.

“If you see unreleased music, products, books, experiences, and campaigns launched through official Dolly Parton channels, you can have confidence in knowing that she placed her personal stamp on it.”
The “9 to 5” singer’s team also shared a video compilation of Parton hard at work, promoting some upcoming content.

Parton’s team also said that details on additional projects, including an avatar show she previously spoke about, a biopic, docuseries, scripted series, a Billy The Kid animated series and many more “will be revealed soon.”

title: Dolly Parton Had a Well-Documented Love Affair With Food. These Were Her Favorites
summary: Dolly Parton loved to cook and eat foods like chicken and dumplings, funnel cake, fried chicken, potatoes (in any form), milk gravy and more Southern staples.
story: Dolly Parton was a meat-and-potatoes kind of woman.
The iconic singer, songwriter, actor and philanthropist died at the age of 80 on Aug. 25 following a “brief battle with cancer,” her estate announced.
Over her spectacularly rhinestone-speckled life, she appeared on TODAY over 50 times, sometimes with a plate full of muffins or a cake in tow.
After Parton’s nephew Bryan Seaver shared the news of her death in an Instagram video, fans shared their condolences — and many of them made food that reminded them of her.

Parton and the Southern food she grew up on were intrinsically linked, leading to several food partnerships, a line of Lodge cooking pans, and two cookbooks from the “9 to 5” singer, including one with her sister, Rachel Parton George.
In those books and in interviews over the years, the “Jolene” singer shared some of her favorite dishes. Here is a selection of them from over the years — a “Coat of Many Colors,” if you will.
Fried Chicken
Parton told TODAY.com more than once that fried chicken was at the top of her family’s favorite foods list.

“Growing up in the South with my mom being the greatest cook in the world — and my aunts and my grandmas — I just remember things like fried chicken on Sunday was one of the greatest things ever,” she told TODAY.com in January 2022.

Later, in September 2024, she said, “I think there’s something about Sundays and fried chicken — even in the country — that was just a special treat … The preacher in our family happened to be our grandpa, and grandpa loved fried chicken.”
Funnel Cake

Dollywood, Parton’s theme park, offers some irresistible foods. From cinnamon bread at The Grist Mill or pot roast at Aunt Granny’s Restaurant, guests could snack on any of a number of Dolly’s delicacies. In January 2025, Parton revealed which food she always has to have when she sets foot in her eponymous park.

“The funnel cakes we’re famous for, so I never go there … even if I’m in my bus or if I’m in my suite, The Dolly Suite, I say, ‘Run and get me some funnel cakes. I can’t leave here without funnel cakes,’” she said.
Banana Pudding, Coconut Cake and Chocolate Cake
Parton stopped by TODAY in 2022 to chat about her line of cake mixes and frostings with Duncan Hines, and shared her love for another dessert.
“Everybody in the South — but everywhere, really — we love bananas, and we love banana pudding,” she said. “When you have a good banana pudding, it’s great.”
She also expressed her adoration for cake during the segment.

“I always think of Sundays when I think of coconut cake,” she said. “My mom always made either chocolate cake or coconut cake on Sundays, but on Easter, we always had a coconut cake. So we just felt that it was really a nice start for me to do something more Southern, and they’re beautiful.”
Milk Gravy
“Every now and then I’ll make my husband, Carl, an extra special breakfast,” she said on TODAY.com in 2020 while sharing her own recipe.
She added that, when she made Southern staples like sausage patties or flaky biscuits for her husband Carl Dean, who died in 2025, she would make an easy, creamy milk gravy as the “perfect” topping.
Get The Recipe
Taco Bell
Parton told Insider in January and April 2022 that when she wasn’t cooking, she and her husband would sometimes hit up Taco Bell.

“I like soft-shell tacos,” Parton said. “I like the others, but they fall apart so bad, especially if you’re riding around. So I always get a Taco Supreme, with the sour cream and all that, in the soft shell. I love that.”
She also revealed she loved the then-discontinued Mexican Pizza, which may have convinced the chain to resurrect the dish in May 2022.
Potatoes, in Any Form
In 2025, she told TODAY.com that every day, she had “to have something with potatoes.”
“I mean, I’m just one of those people that I have to either have a baked potato, some mashed potatoes, or some french fries, or something to do with potatoes,” Parton told TODAY.com.
Earlier, in 2022, she also said she enjoys the tuberous starch at barbecues, in the form of a mayo-based potato salad, along with a vinegar-based coleslaw.

“When that happened at our church, and that big bowl of potato salad got there, you didn’t have to worry,” she said. “Even it was sunny, it wasn’t gonna last that long! It wasn’t gonna go bad … not if I was around!”
Chicken and Dumplings and Peanut Butter Fudge

Chicken and Dumplings, which appears in her recipe book, “Good Lookin’ Cookin,’” was also a favorite on the movie sets she graced. She would also whip up a sweet treat that co-stars like Lily Tomlin or Jane Fonda may have snacked on while filming “9 to 5”: peanut butter fudge.

“I cook a lot when I’m on my movie sets,” she said in 2022. “So I guess it would be a long list of famous people, because whoever the stars and co-stars are. I have this huge big pot, and I make chicken and dumplings. I’m famous for it, so everybody wants me to make that or a peanut butter fudge that I love and take on set with me. Everybody asks, ‘When are you going to do the dumplings?’ I always announce it a couple of days before so they all look forward to it. So, I’ve had my dumplings eaten by a lot of famous people.”

title: Tim Curry Was the World’s Scariest Clown. It Surprised Him Until the Very End
summary: Tim Curry was terrifying playing the clown Pennywise in “IT,” the 1990 TV-movie adaptation of Stephen King’s book.
story: Coulrophobia is the fear of clowns. There is, however, no known name for the specific condition of coulrophobia, as brought on by Tim Curry.
Curry, of course, may have generated more than a few cases of coulrophobia all by himself, thanks to one of his most memorable parts.
The actor’s manager shared on Aug. 26 that he had died at the age of 80.
In 1990, Curry took on a role that was as frightening as something you would read in a Stephen King book, which is not a coincidence because it came from a Stephen King book.

In “IT,” based on King’s 1986 book of the same name, Curry portrayed Pennywise, the demonic clown terrorizing a group of child outcasts in 1960s Maine, and resurfaces decades later to wreak more havoc.

“IT” was a four-hour movie that aired over two nights. Curry was the linchpin of the film, which also starred John Ritter, Tim Reid, Richard Thomas, Harry Anderson, Annette O’Toole, as well as child stars Jonathan Brandis and Seth Green.
Pennywise is as scary as scary can be, and Curry was often taken aback at the effect the character had long after the movie aired.

“The majority of people who want to talk to me about being Pennywise are either notably odd people, who sort of revel in his evilness, or else they want me to know that I’ve really traumatized them, or made it impossible to sleep, or something of that variety,” he wrote in his 2025 memoir, “Vagabond.”
“I don’t blame them — one of my lines is literally ‘I’m your worst dream come true.’ But I’ve never really known how to respond to that.”
Curry, who already had a following for his work in “The Rocky Horror Picture Show” and “Clue,” seemed to have mixed feelings about “IT,” which was remade for the big screen in 2017.

“I haven’t had much to say about it publicly for many years, which many people misread as my carrying some sort of deep conflict about the role,” he wrote in “Vagabond.” “That’s really not the case, but I didn’t revel in the role, either.”
Imagine, though, if Curry did revel in it. He was mesmerizing in his portrayal of the clown who lured in children with his menacing smile and balloons.

“My job was to give Tim the stage and not get in his way too much,” “IT” director Tommy Lee Wallace told The Hollywood Reporter in 2017. “He was like Robin Williams in the way he brought a spontaneous improvisation to the part.”

This was transcendental stuff. Curry reached a level of terror that the slasher films of the ‘80s aspired to — and he did it in a TV movie that preyed on the visceral over the physical. It would’ve been right at home had people coughed up a few bucks to see it on the big screen.
“Beep beep, Richie.”
“They all float down here.”
“I’m every nightmare you’ve ever had. I’m your worst dream come true. I’m everything you ever were afraid of.”
If you’ve seen the movie, you can see and hear Curry delivering those lines. They still echo more than three decades later.
The Hollywood Reporter applauded the film, calling it “one big kicky ride thanks to the charismatic acting of Curry as savage, sneering malevolence.”

“I don’t like clowns. I never did,” he told The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences earlier this year. “But I liked doing that show a lot because you have immense freedom, really, as a clown.”

Curry was so on point that he recalled scaring Tony Dakota, one of his co-stars, in a scene that takes place early in the movie when Georgie (played by Dakota) chases his toy boat after it goes into the sewer, where Pennywise is holed up.

“He stopped in the middle of the scene and said, ‘Mr. Curry, you’re scaring me.’ I said, ‘Well, ‘I’m supposed to scare you, but I don’t mean to harm you in any way,” he told The Academy, echoing a story he also shared in “Vagabond.”

“IT” earned two Emmy nominations, winning one for outstanding achievement in music composition for a miniseries or a special. It was also nominated for best editing. It’s amazing to think that Curry did not earn a nomination, given the enduring nature of the part.

Interestingly, Curry would earn one Emmy in his career — and it was connected to horror. He garnered a nod in 1994 for outstanding guest actor in a drama series for appearing on the HBO anthology series “Tales from the Crypt.”

Curry called “IT” “very original, very audacious, and yes, legitimately frightening” in “Vagabond.” He would go on to write that fans often ask him to do Pennywise’s voice when he goes to conventions, which he called “a weird phenomenon.” It shows the power of the part and the connection fans still feel to this very day.
“I never would have imagined that out of my whole body of work, that clown would end up being so memorable to audiences,” he wrote.

title: Bob Barker Reflects on 3 Decades of Hosting ‘The Price Is Right’ in 2002 TODAY Interview
summary: On April 1, 2002, Bob Barker stopped by TODAY to look back at his experiences, a mere 30 years into his tenure.
story: Welcome inside the TODAY Vault, where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment aired April 1, 2002 and features Bob Barker talking to Al Roker about “The Price is Right” 30 years into his run as host of the beloved game show.
The history of game shows can’t be told without Bob Barker.
Barker, who helped make “The Price is Right” a staple of daytime television during his 35-year run as host, died Aug. 26, 2023, at the age of 99.
He began his stint on the show in 1972 and remained on the job until 2007, a vital part in turning the show into the smash hit it remains to this day with current host Drew Carey.
On April 1, 2002, Barker stopped by TODAY to look back at his experiences, a mere 30 years into his tenure.
“Sometimes it seems much longer,” he said while laughing. “And sometimes it seems like only yesterday that we started.”
Barker also spoke about what had changed over the years, why young people loved the show and how he broke into the business.
How Had ‘The Price is Right’ Changed Since He Began Hosting?
Barker noted that the set remained the same, but the cost of the items on the show had evolved.

“The prices, that’s what has really changed,” he said. “The first car I gave away was $2,465. We had car after car, four digits. Two was the first number. Then 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Now we’ve had to change our props to accommodate five digits.”
‘The Price is Right’ Appealed to Young People

It’s lore that kids watched the show when they stayed home sick from school. That love didn’t dissipate over time, either, as evidenced by the young people and college students who appear on the show. Barker couldn’t explain why a younger demographic was so drawn to the series, but he was glad it was.
“We’re blessed. It happened. We don’t know how it happened. If we did, we could bottle it and sell it. But it became a cult thing with the college youngsters,” he said.
“And now they come from all over the country — East Coast, Midwest, and, of course, the West Coast — and they give our show great energy. It’s just wonderful,” he added.
How Did Bob Barker Wind Up Hosting Game Shows?

Prior to “The Price is Right,” Barker hosted “Truth or Consequences” for 18 years. He began his career in radio and ultimately made the move to the small screen with encouragement from his wife, Dorothy Jo Gideon.
“I started working at a radio station when I was in college. They didn’t call them game shows. They were audience participation shows,” he said.

“The first audience participation show I did, my wife heard and she said, ‘That’s what you should do.’ She said, ‘You do that better than you’ve ever done anything else.’ Now she didn’t say I was good,” he joked. “She just said I did it better than I’ve ever done anything else. And I set out to do precisely what I’m doing.”

title: Young Dolly Parton Photos: See the ‘Queen of Country’ Through the Years
summary: See pictures of Dolly Parton from the earlier part of her life as a child into adulthood when she posed with some huge stars.
story: The world continues to mourn Dolly Parton’s death of cancer at the age of 80.

Tributes for the icon — who was a TODAY staple and sage speaker — have poured in from across all corners, as the global superstar leaves behind a legacy in which she was known not just for her music and acting, but for her humility and generosity.

Parton was married to Carl Dean for 60 years before his death in 2025. There was another Dolly Parton, though, long before they tied the knot and long before she became a worldwide superstar who wrote over 3,000 songs.

Parton was Dolly Rebecca Parton on Jan. 19, 1946, the fourth of 12 children. She grew up in rural Sevierville, Tennessee and sang on local television and radio while still a child. At 13, Johnny Cash introduced her for her 1959 debut at the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville.

Stardom awaited her. Parton moved to Nashville to pursue a music career after graduating high school in 1964. In 1967, country star and TV personality Porter Wagoner handpicked her to be his new duet partner on “The Porter Wagoner Show.”

That same year, she released her debut solo album, “Hello, I’m Dolly,” which rose to the number 11 spot on the Billboard Top Country Albums chart and announced her arrival as a star for years to come.
Take a look at Parton throughout her younger years below.
Dolly Parton From Her 1st Recording to Co-Starring with Porter Wagoner
Parton’s first single, “Puppy Love,” came out in 1955, when Parton was about 9 years old. When she was 21, Wagoner offered her a life-changing spot on his syndicated show.
Dolly Parton Went Solo in 1974 and Became a Star

Parton became a solo act and rocketed to stardom in the 1970s, propelled, in part, by the success of her songs “Joshua,” “Coat of Many Colors,” “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You.” Those tracks would remain some of her signature songs throughout her career.
Dolly Parton Hobnobbed With Celebrities for Years

As her star rose, so did her profile. Parton was not known for appearing in the tabloids, but she did cross paths with several stars over the years as she crossed into the mainstream by making the jump into film with ‘9 to 5” in 1980. Even before that, she had emerged as a superstar.

title: Miley Cyrus Honors Late Godmother Dolly Parton After Her Death: ‘I Have an Angel By My Side’
summary: Singer Miley Cyrus shared a heartfelt tribute after the passing of her “fairy godmother,” Dolly Parton.
story: To the world, Dolly Parton was a country music legend. To Miley Cyrus, she was her “fairy godmother.”
Parton’s nephew shared that she died “peacefully” on Aug. 25 at the age of 80. And today on Instagram, Cyrus gave Parton her “flowers.”

“The feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share. Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour & between our hearts,” she began.

“What I KNOW is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis. 🦋

“I will always love her and want to make her proud. My heart breaks for the world, her family and friends who will miss her deeply. We’re in this loss together and we will see her in all of the most beautiful things. 💖”

Parton had a long-standing friendship with the singer’s parents, Billy Ray Cyrus and Tish Cyrus-Purcell, and she shared the story of becoming a godmother during an interview in 2023 on SiriusXM’s “The Howard Stern Show.”

“We just got to be good friends because he’s a Kentucky boy, I’m from Tennessee,” Parton said at the time. “And he said … ‘We’re having a girl, and you’ve got to be her godmother!’ And I said, ‘Well, I’d be honored.’ So actually, Miley and I took over from there.”
Miley Cyrus and Dolly Parton have a long history of gushing over one another, both personally and professionally.

They collaborated in front of the cameras when Parton guest starred on three episodes of “Hannah Montana” as her character’s fictional on-screen godmother. And together they sang Parton’s 1973 hit “Jolene” with Pentatonix on “The Voice” in 2016.
When Parton was honored by as one of Time’s Most Influential People of 2021, Cyrus wrote a tribute to her.

“There’s a theory that you shouldn’t meet your heroes, but I wish everyone had the chance to meet Dolly Parton, because she’s even better than your sparkliest dreams,” Cyrus wrote. “She may be my fairy godmother, but I think she’s that to everyone else too. I am happy to share her with the world.”
Cyrus shared a message that her godmother sent her a few years later.
“Dolly’s been like a mother to me. Actually, I was just reading this fax that she sent me two Mother’s Days ago,” Cyrus told W Magazine in 2024.
“Dolly wrote to me to say: ‘How much do I love you? As much as my heart can hold and as far as my arms can reach,’” Cyrus recalled. “It gets me choked up. I just love her so much.”
In a Facebook tribute, Billy Ray Cyrus said that he grew up watching Parton on his living room TV, and shared a memory from a meeting with her in 1992.

“I’ll never forget walking into her dressing room to apologize for all the tabloid stories which claimed I was having an affair with her. In true Dolly fashion, she just looked at me, winked and said, ‘Honey, this trash sells records!’” Billy Ray Cyrus wrote.
The singer added that Parton recently sent him a message telling him that she “loved me with her whole heart.”
“I will always love her in the same way ….. with my whole heart … and I always will,” he said.

title: TODAY Anchors Honor Dolly Parton and Her Life Spent Spreading Joy: ‘She Was an Original’
summary: Following the death of beloved country music icon Dolly Parton, the TODAY family took a trip down memory lane to reflect on the many ways she had touched their lives.
story: Following the death of beloved country music icon Dolly Parton, the TODAY family took a trip down memory lane to reflect on the many ways she had touched their lives.
“It goes without saying how much we love Dolly Parton,” Hoda Kotb said on TODAY Aug. 26. “Her music was the soundtrack of so many lives, and that’s just one small part of her incredible legacy.”
Carson Daly highlighted the “rhinestone-studded trail” Parton had blazed for countless entertainers who had followed her, many of whom had shared their personal tributes to Parton.

“It’s crazy, from all walks of life ... all genres of music,” Carson said of the music industry’s admiration for Parton. He recalled how she initially turned down her nomination for the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame because she didn’t feel her music was worthy. Parton later accepted the nomination — and then she proceeded to put out a rock album in 2023.

“I don’t think she cared about any accolades,” Hoda said. “It was as if the accolades didn’t mean much to her because she often said, ‘If I didn’t get paid or if I wasn’t that good, I would still be singing.’”
Kristen Welker also shared about Parton’s legacy, including what her fans meant to her.

“She was just so humble,” Kristen said, reflecting on Parton’s response when asked if she felt bothered when people recognized her. “She said, ‘Are you kidding? That’s why I’m here.’ She loved just being with the people and spreading that love.”
Craig Melvin highlighted Parton’s family background, being one of 12 children, as a possible source of her humility.
Carson then chimed in, further commemorating Parton’s reach.

“Country music was regional, it was walled off of mainstream,” he said. “She comes in and owns her masters, she owns her likeness, she owns her rights. She’s a business savant. ... And by the way, her greatest legacy might be what she’s done for literacy.”

Parton founded the Imagination Library, a book gifting program that grants young children around the country access to free books. Carson continued to list Parton’s contributions to society beyond entertaining, including her donations to fund a COVID vaccine and helping those impacted by natural disasters.
“She didn’t want the accolades,” Carson said. “She wanted to help.”
Later on TODAY, “9 to 5” played on the Plaza, with Craig shouting out Parton as a “national treasure.”
Hoda, who has interviewed Parton many times, reflected on a moment when Parton made an impact on another member of the TODAY family, Megan Stackhouse, who is head of public relations.

“She walked up to Dolly and said, ‘You raised me.’” Hoda remembered. “And Dolly enveloped her, hugged her, and I remember Megan crying. We all got to sit and chat with her, but those are the moments I think stick out the most for me.”

title: What To Know About Dolly Parton’s Relationship With Goddaughter Miley Cyrus
