summary: Dolly Parton agreed to be godmother to Miley Cyrus before the “Hannah Montana” star was born. Discover all their is to know about their deep bond.
story: Successful in both music and film, the late Dolly Parton also took on the role of godmother to singer and actor Miley Cyrus.

Parton was “honored” to take on the task when Cyrus’ father, fellow country music star Billy Ray, asked her to ahead of Cyrus’ birth, Parton recalled during a 2023 appearance on “The Howard Stern Show.” “So actually, Miley and I took over from there. We just stayed very, very close through the years.”
The two have collaborated on stage, acted together and revealed details about their shared inner life throughout Cyrus’ upbringing.
Never having had children, Parton said she was able to be “everybody’s mother” in a 1984 interview, a benefit for which Cyrus often expressed gratitude.

“Dolly’s been like a mother to me. Actually, I was just reading this fax that she sent me two Mother’s Days ago,” Cyrus told W Magazine in 2024. “Dolly wrote to me to say: ‘How much do I love you? As much as my heart can hold and as far as my arms can reach,’” Cyrus said. “It gets me choked up. I just love her so much.”
The two musical icons had long shared a loving bond. Ahead, what to know about their relationship.
Parton Has Known Cyrus Since ‘Before She Was Born’
On “The Howard Stern Show,” Parton explained that she became close to Cyrus’ father when he toured with her while promoting his 1992 single, “Achy Breaky Heart.”

“We just got to be good friends because he’s a Kentucky boy, I’m from Tennessee,” Parton said. “And he said … ‘We’re having a girl, and you’ve got to be her godmother!’ And I said, ‘Well, I’d be honored.’”
Parton also described her goddaughter as her “little sweetheart,” adding: “I’ve known her since before she was born, actually.”
Parton Guest-Starred on ‘Hannah Montana’
Parton played Aunt Dolly on three episodes of “Hannah Montana.” She appeared in 2006’s “Good Golly, Miss Dolly,” 2007’s “I Will Always Loathe You,” and 2010’s “Kiss It All Goodbye.”
The country legend said she felt like a “proud mama” as she worked with her young goddaughter on the hit Disney Channel series.
“I was so proud of her. I thought she was sensational,” Parton told Vanity Fair in 2020.

“We just worked so great together. ... And thanks to her, I had a whole new following of people that were turned on to me,” she also said. “These young, little kids that were her fans, and kids that were fans of just the whole show, and the other little artists on the show, but here I am, Miley’s fairy godmother.”
In a 2021 essay for Time magazine, Cyrus reflected on working with Parton on “Hannah Montana.”

“I remember when she came in to do a table read for ‘Hannah Montana’ in all her bedazzled glory. Her smell, the way her nails tapped the table, the sound it made when she flipped the pages of the script — I could see that she fascinated other people too,” Cyrus wrote. “A living fantasy was in front of all of us.”
They Have Collaborated on Music

Cyrus and Parton teamed up to co-host NBC’s “Miley’s New Year’s Eve Party” and ring in 2023. They performed duets of two of their greatest ballads: Cyrus’ ”Wrecking Ball” and Parton’s “I Will Always Love You.”
Parton opened up about the emotional experience of performing with her goddaughter.
“Even when we were rehearsing, Miley was crying,” Parton told Business Insider in 2023.

“The fact that we were singing so well together stirred up our emotions very much,” she added. “Then we went into ‘I Will Always Love You’ and she would just have these tears coming down and it was so emotional.”
Parton and Cyrus also performed a cover of “Wrecking Ball” for Parton’s rock album, “Rockstar,” which came out in November 2023.
This version features a playful change to the lyrics, a nod to Parton’s “I Will Always Love You.”

In the original version of “Wrecking Ball,” Cyrus sings, “I can’t live a lie, running for my life/ I will always want you,” but in the collaboration with Parton, the line is changed to, “I can’t live a lie, running for my life/ I will always love you.”

Cyrus celebrated this collaboration with her godmother in a post on X: “I’ve grown up covering my Aunt Dollys music & it’s an honor to hear her singing one of my songs,” she wrote. “I love you Aunt Dolly! I’m so happy to add another collaboration under our bedazzled (studded leather) belt!”
Parton Is One of Cyrus’ Biggest Cheerleaders
Parton has always jumped at the chance to sing her goddaughter’s praises, both professionally and personally.
The country legend called Cyrus “smart and talented” in an essay she penned when Cyrus was named one of Time magazine’s 100 Most Influential People in 2014.

“She knows what she’s doing. She was very proud of the work she did as Hannah Montana, but people were gonna leave her there forever,” she wrote. “And she was just smotherin’ and chokin’ in it. So she felt she had to do something completely drastic. And she did. She made her point, she made her mark, and more power to her.”
In 2020, Parton spoke to Vanity Fair about Cyrus forging her own path and pointed out their similarities.

“But you know, she’s like me. She’s finding her own space, she’s finding her own things, and she’ll always land on her feet,” Parton said. “I don’t always have to agree with everything she does, but it ain’t my business. That’s her life. I’m just her fairy godmother, and I love her.”
She also praised her goddaughter when Howard Stern asked if Cyrus ever came to her for advice.

“Well, she’s asked me a lot of things. She mostly just runs things by me, and we talk,” she said. “She’s very successful. Miley’s very smart. She’s very intuitive about the business, and I just think Miley’s a spectacular human being and an amazing talent.”
Cyrus Said Parton Is Her ‘Idol’

“Have you ever met anyone who doesn’t love Dolly Parton? I never have,” Cyrus wrote in an essay about Parton when Parton was honored on the Time 100 list in 2021. “Dolly is not only my idol because of her incomparable career — she’s also my role model because of her steadfast morals and values.”
“There’s a theory that you shouldn’t meet your heroes, but I wish everyone had the chance to meet Dolly Parton, because she’s even better than your sparkliest dreams,” Cyrus also wrote.
In her W magazine interview, Cyrus also mentioned thinking about her godmother as she reflected on having children someday.
“I’m 31 now, and I still don’t know if I want kids or not,” she said at the time. “I feel like my fans kind of are my kids in some way. I’ve heard Dolly say that too, because she didn’t have kids.”
Their bond runs deep on stage and off.

“There’s a chemistry, and a realness, and a love, and a connection that her and I have that I really feel,” Cyrus told TODAY ahead of their New Year’s Eve performance in 2022. “You can see our chemistry, and I really don’t think there’s much to write. There’s not much to choreograph. It’s all right there,” she added.
Parton Taught Cyrus to Dream Big
Cyrus credits the 20th anniversary special for “Hannah Montana,” which aired in 2026, to Parton.

Ahead of official announcements for the special, Cyrus teased something was in the works during interviews. Turns out, the special hadn’t yet been greenlit. But Cyrus took a page from Parton’s book and spoke it into existence.

“I learned this terrible habit — but I actually think it was good advice — from Dolly,” Cyrus told Variety. “She told me that if you want something to happen, promote it before it exists. Then no one can say ‘no.’ So I just started promoting a ‘Hannah Montana’ 20th-anniversary special that literally did not exist.”
They Both Worked With Beyoncé on the “Cowboy Carter” Album
When Parton allowed Beyoncé to cover her music on Beyoncé’s first country album, Parton revealed she didn’t imagine Beyoncé would pick “Jolene.”

When E! News asked about the choice, Parton said, “Well, I think it was very bold of her. When they said she was going to do ‘Jolene,’ I expected it to be my regular one, but it wasn’t. But I love what she did to it.”

Parton was happy with the rendition. In fact, Parton praised Beyoncé’s lyric changes, too. In Beyoncé’s version, she warns Jolene to stay away from her man, unlike Parton’s original in which she begs Jolene not to take her man.

Cyrus collaborated with Beyoncé on the same album, lending her voice to the song, “II Most Wanted.” When the album was released, Cyrus sang Beyoncé’s praises. “I’ve loved Beyoncé since long before I had the opportunity to meet & work with her,” Cyrus wrote on Instagram. “My admiration runs so much deeper now that I’ve created along side of her. Thank you Beyoncé. You’re everything & more. Love you.”

She also performed the duet during the Paris leg of Beyoncé’s Cowboy Carter tour. “To have learned from you & loved you my whole life, & then be standing together in matching gold looks is more than I could’ve imagined,” Cyrus wrote on social media.
Cyrus and Parton Are Actually Related

While they already considered each other family, Cyrus and Parton are, in fact, actually related, according to Cosmopolitan. The outlet cited a 2024 Ancestry.com report that states the two stars were seventh cousins.
Parton and Cyrus, the genealogy site found, shared an ancestor who was Parton’s sixth great-grandfather and Cyrus’ seventh great-grandfather.

title: Dolly Parton Once Showed TODAY’s Willie Geist How She Wrote ‘9 to 5’ Using Her Fingernails
summary: During a 2020 interview with Willie Geist, Country legend, Dolly Parton, revealed how she used her acrylic fingernails to help pen her No. 1 hit “9 to 5.”
story: “The Queen of Country” is gone, but Dolly Parton leaves behind a lasting legacy of music, generosity and a catalog of hit songs. Among the most memorable is Parton’s No. 1 hit “9 to 5.”

The 1980 tune was written for the movie by the same name featuring Parton, Lily Tomlin and Jane Fonda. The trio starred as Doralee, Violet and Judy, three beleaguered secretaries working for sexist boss Franklin Hart Jr. (Dabney Coleman).
After suffering at the hands of their boss’s relentless demands, they hatch a plan to exact their revenge, and it doesn’t go quite as planned.

While the movie was one of the biggest box-office successes of the year, it was Parton’s song that took home all the awards, earning two Grammys and an Oscar nod, along with spending 26 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100.
Four decades later, it still remains one of the most popular anthems dedicated to the grind of the 9-to-5 worker.
What might be the most interesting fact about the toe-tapper, however, is that it was written, in part, on Parton’s fingernails.
In a 2020 interview with TODAY’s Willie Geist, Parton explained that she penned the hit song while on the set of the movie, but since she didn’t have an instrument, she had to improvise.
“I did it on my fingernails,” Parton tells Willie, scratching her legendary long nails together. “Can you hear that?” she asks, of the rhythmic tapping.

“They sound like a typewriter,” she explained. “I didn’t have my guitar because I didn’t want to get too scattered because we were trying to stay in the mood, and they were doing lights and all that. So, I would just look around and I would get ideas watching whatever was going on on the set.”

As she pondered the song, she says thought about the movie’s storyline; women in the workplace, their race to get out of the house in morning and Parton began tapping out the song’s iconic beat on her nails, washboard style.
“I would just kind of play my little fingers, go back to the hotel at night, write down the words, get my guitar and start singing it,” she recalls. “That’s how it all kind of how that all worked.”
Even though her fingernails were intended as a placeholder for her guitar, the nail-scratching ultimately made it into the final cut of “9 to 5.”

“I played my nails on the real record just for fun because all the girls got a kick out of me singing it to them, running around,” said Parton laughing. “Even Jane (Fonda) and Lily (Tomlin), to this day, every time they see me, they start going (scratching nails together).”
Even so, there’s one caveat, Parton explained. “You’ve got to have acrylic nails though, which I don’t think either of them do, so they don’t play it as good as I do.”

Penning “9 to 5” wasn’t the only time Parton used her fingernails to tap out a tune, either. The Queen of Country memorably performed a nail duet in 1987 with Grammy-winning singer Patti LaBelle on her variety show “Dolly.”

Telling LaBelle that she often tapped out songs on the dashboard of her car when she didn’t have a guitar on hand, Parton invited to singer to join her in singing the classic folk song “Shortnin’ Bread.”
Together, the pair harmonized and scratched their nails in unison. “That’s cute!” said LaBelle of their acrylic collaboration. “We did plan this, but we didn’t know how it was going to sound.”
LaBelle wrapped the brief but iconic moment with a quick nail solo before the pair finished to cheers and applause.

Parton’s “9 to 5” co-stars paid tribute to their long-time friend upon Parton’s passing on Aug. 25 at the age of 80, with Tomlin posting on X, “Friend. Songwriter. The Great Harmonizer of Humanity. Dolly. Dolly. Dolly. Forever Dolly.”

Fonda honored Parton with a long post on Instagram, writing, “More than anyone I have ever known, Dolly will always be with us because she was so present, so powerful, so generous and playful that she is woven into all our lives and hearts forever.”

Fonda summed up her friend’s legacy by saying, “We have our memories of her, her songs, Dollywood, ‘9to5,’ the millions of books she got into the hands of children, all the iconic images that bring her to us. And they are all blessings.”

title: Eminem Shares Letter Dolly Parton Once Wrote Him About Their ‘Unexplained Connection,’ Despite Never Meeting
summary: Among all the tributes to Dolly Parton in the wake of her death, Eminem’s post truly illustrates how she touched people across all walks of life.
story: Among all the tributes to Dolly Parton in the wake of her death, one of them truly illustrates how she touched people across all walks of life.
“Jolene” and “The Real Slim Shady” may have been far apart musically, but even Eminem had a heartfelt remembrance of a time the country icon reached out with some kind words for him.

The legendary rapper, whose real name is Marshall Mathers, shared a thoughtful note on Instagram that Parton sent him following his induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022. It was one of many tributes to Parton following the announcement of her death at 80 on Aug. 25.

“I’m sorry we never got a chance to meet, but getting this note from Dolly really had an impact on me,” he wrote. “She definitely didn’t have to take the time to do it. Even for a kid who mostly listened to rap music, she was an icon. A superstar in every sense. Rest easy Dolly. And thank you for the kind words.”

Parton was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame herself as part of the same class of inductees as Eminem in 2022. Parton sang her iconic hit “Jolene” and Eminem performed a medley of his most memorable songs as part of the induction ceremony.

“Congratulations on your induction to the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame,” she wrote in her note. “Your performance was amazing and everybody said so. Even though I don’t know a lot about rap music, I’ve come to know that you are the very best at it.”

The two performers, who are 27 years apart in age, shared similar hardscrabble upbringings and success as underdogs in the music industry. They are also synonymous with their roots — Parton in Tennessee and Eminem in Detroit.

“Aside from that I hope what I have to say will not seem weird or strange to you but I have always felt some unexplained connection to you like I know you somehow,” Parton wrote in her note. “I had hoped to meet you at the show but you know how nuts those things are, personally I hate ‘em and I missed my chance but maybe someday we’ll meet.
“In the meantime, keep doing what you’re doing because you do it so well and no matter how complex your world may be just know you are very special and touch people in ways you don’t even know.”
Parton signed the letter, “With love & respect.”

In addition to tributes from her peers, Parton also received an outpouring of love from younger artists who respected and collaborated with her over the years. Taylor Swift, Beyoncé, Sabrina Carpenter and goddaughter Miley Cyrus were all artists who had a strong connection to the 80-year-old legend.

title: Taylor Swift Remembers Dolly Parton’s ‘True Grace and True Grit’ in Statement After Her Death
summary: Taylor Swift paid tribute to Dolly Parton in a heartfelt statement written after her death.
story: Taylor Swift paid tribute to Dolly Parton’s “everlasting” legacy and example of “true grace and grit” following the country music legend’s death at 80 years old.
The global pop star joined a host of other music luminaries in remembering Parton after the singer’s family announced on Aug. 25 that she died after a “brief battle with cancer.”
Swift, whom Parton praised in a video at the 2023 iHeartRadio Music Awards, released a statement in the wake of her death.

“A world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right,” she said. “But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one.”
Swift, 36, was one of several female pop stars decades younger than Parton whom the country star befriended, including Beyoncé, Sabrina Carpenter and goddaughter Miley Cyrus.

“She was truly the gift that kept on giving,” Swift continued. “Dolly gave us someone to look up to while encouraging us to be who we are as individuals. Somehow she was able to give us her lessons about the world gently and honestly, simultaneously, and oftentimes hilariously. She managed to give the world the ultimate mystery and fantasy in some corners of her life, but to give full transparency in the ways that counted. Somehow she was true grace and true grit, all in one dazzling person. She possessed the softest heart when it came to the struggles of others, and a backbone of steel to defend her own self worth as an artist.”
Swift also noted Parton’s extensive philanthropic work, which included founding the Imagination Library. The organization has donated hundreds of millions of books to support child literacy.

“Along with her other fans, I am so grateful for all of it,” Swift said. “For the melodies and lyrics she wrote that thawed even the coldest hearts. For the millions of books she provided children all over the world so that they might fall in love with stories the way she did. For the tightropes she walked so that young girls like me could grow up dreaming of joining the circus too.
“Dolly, I’ll think of you each step of the way.”

title: Dolly Parton Visited TODAY More Than 50 Times. See Her Best Performances, Jokes and ‘Dollyisms’
summary: Dolly Parton was a frequent guest on TODAY over the years. Look back at some of her most memorable moments.
story: Dolly Parton, who died after a battle with cancer, on Aug. 25 at the age of 80, was a frequent guest on TODAY over the years, showcasing her trademark wit and big heart for viewers to see.

“I’m always happy to be on the TODAY show!” she said during a 2025 interview with Savannah Guthrie and Craig Melvin, in a spot where Savannah reminded her that she had been on the show more than 50 times.
The icon’s run of appearances began Aug. 23, 1978, and would span six decades. Her first sit-down interview was with then co-host Jane Pauley.

“I want to tell you, too, I think you’re great, and every time I’m up that early in the morning I watch you. And my husband’s watching you now,” she said, referencing her husband Carl Dean, who died in 2025.

She’s also brought her legendary pipes to the show. She took over the plaza in heels and a bright red dress for a concert in 2002 where she sang one of her trademark songs, “9 to 5,” from the movie of the same name. In 2016, she performed a dazzling rendition of “Coat of Many Colors” in a Studio 1A lit up with a rainbow.

When Dolly stopped by the show, memorable moments often followed. During a 2019 interview, everyone in the control room wore Dolly wigs, causing her to squeal in delight. That same year, she also sang “Jolene” as a duet with Hoda Kotb, with Savannah Guthrie accompanying on guitar.
“I think you girls are behind. You better stick to your hosting!” Parton joked at the time.
From the beginning, Parton also brought her unique vernacular with her.
“My momma always said that any old barn looked better with a little red paint on it,” she told Pauley with a laugh during that first 1978 interview.
“I’m out there hustling! That’s one of the reasons I’m out, I’m not going to go down on a sinking ship without looking for a dingy!” she also joked during a 1993 appearance.
Calling in to chat with Hoda and Jenna Bush Hager in 2022, she spoke frankly, joking about rumors she had certain body parts insured.
“Well, it’s not true. You can get new boobs, but you can’t get new legs,” she said.

Parton was also known for being humble. She initially declined her nomination for the Rock & Rock Hall of Fame in 2022. Her interviews showcased her modest attitude, and she often shared the secrets to her success. In 2019, she said the song “9 to 5” came to life simply because of her nails.
“I have my nails, too, my acrylic nails. That’s how I wrote ‘9 to 5’ on the set of ‘9 to 5,’” she said, confirming to Willie Geist in 2020 she actually “played” her nails on the record.
Parton, of course, was more than just music. She promoted childhood literacy with her Imagination Library, giving books to children all over the world.
“We’re trying to teach children to love books, to learn to read early,” she said during a 2000 interview.
Parton also brought a humanity with her, expressing her hopes that people be the best versions of themselves.

“Can’t we rise above? Can’t we show some love? Can’t we just lift up? And just help each other out?” she said in December 2022. “I’m going to try my best to try to bring as much joy as I can and lift people up as much as I can.”
Parton’s faith was on display during her TODAY appearances.
“I love everybody, I try to find the God light in everybody, and we all have it,” she said in May 2019.
In November 2019, she opened up about her own relationship with God.
“I just always had, with my conversations with God, I’d just ask him every day, as I still do, to lead me and guide me,” she said.
While Parton was known for her big hair and bright clothing, even in her first interview, she knew she wanted to be known for more than that.
“If they can see behind all this garbage, and if they can appreciate the music, and if they can appreciate me as a person, then that’s all I care about,” she said in 1978.

title: Tributes Pour in for Dolly Parton After Music Legend’s Death at Age 80
summary: The world is mourning the loss of country music legend Dolly Parton who died at age 82. Read tributes and reactions from Reba McEntire, Lily Tomlin and more.
story: The world is mourning the loss of beloved country music star Dolly Parton, who died Aug. 25 at a hospital in Nashville, according to her team. She was 80.

Her death comes a few weeks after she provided an update on her health in a video on Aug. 16 after she missed an event at Dollywood, telling fans, “Sometimes I get a little dizzy and I get dehydrated.”
The “Jolene” singer, who dealt with kidney stones earlier this year, also promised to keep active.
“All has gone well on the medical end of things, and I continue working away on all of our other projects,” she said.

Parton was a giant not just in country music, but entertainment as a whole, releasing her debut album, “Hello, I’m Dolly,” in 1967 before going on to win multiple Grammys and making the leap to the big screen, appearing in classics like the 1980 comedy “9 to 5” and 1989’s “Steel Magnolias.”
Here’s a look at how some famous friends are mourning her death.
Patti LaBelle
Parton used to famously use her acrylic fingernails to create rhythm for her music, and that includes a time when she and Patti LaBelle did it on her variety show, “Dolly,” in the ‘80s.
In a statement to NBC News, LaBelle remembered Parton’s “artistry” and “extraordinary life.”

“I am deeply saddened by the loss of my dear friend who was loved by all. Dolly’s artistry, brilliance, and extraordinary life inspired so many people, including me. Her light will forever shine! I send my deepest condolences to all of her loved ones and fans all over the world!”
Reba McEntire
Fellow country music legend and close friend Reba McEntire penned a tribute on X.

“Well, I just got the news that my buddy Dolly passed onto the higher and greater side,” she began. “Dolly, thank you for all the wonderful things you did for us here on earth. Your love, your music and you gave so much with your huge huge heart.”
She continued, “There will never ever be another you. We will remember and cherish every memory and every note you ever played and sang.”
McEntire said she knows Parton will be in heaven singing her favorite songs with all her loved ones.
“I’ll never forget the first time I met you and I’ll never forget our last conversation. I hold it with love in my heart. I will always love you, Reba,” she concluded.
Jenna Bush Hager

Jenna Bush Hager, who spoke with Parton on several occasions in interviews for TODAY, posted photos to Instagram on Aug. 25, along with a heartfelt message. Two of the photos show Jenna with Dolly during a conversation they had in Dollywood in 2019. At the time, Jenna said, her grandmother Jenna Welch had just passed away.

“As I write this, Dolly’s music is being played in the restaurant where I am eating,” Jenna said. “She was a legend. Her voice was unparalleled, but it was her utter originality and purity of spirit that will be sorely missed. We needed all that glitter and goodness. She gave with all that she was. In this picture of us, I had just recieved the news my grandmother, Jenna had passed away. I was already with her in Knoxville so she held me and gave me such grace. I’ll never forget that kindness. May we take just a little of her beauty and pass it on.
Dionne Warwick
Music icon Dionne Warwick uploaded a picture of her and Parton holding hands on stage together as they performed their duet “Peace Like a River.”
“I will certainly miss her laugher, jokes and her being. Rest well and in total peace my friend. My heart is heavy,” Warwick said.
Dollywood
The leader of Dollywood, the theme park near Knoxville, Tennessee, that attracts Parton’s legions of fans, issued a statement on Aug. 25 to NBC News.

The greatest privilege of my life has been helping Dolly bring her dreams to life at Dollywood,” Eugene Naughton, Dollywood Parks & Resorts President, said. “Dolly’s heart was as vast as the mountains she cherished, and her compassion knew no bounds. She inspired generations to dream boldly and love deeply. While we grieve her loss, we are honored and committed to carry her light forward. Her legacy will continue to shine in every melody sung, every smile shared and every dream kindled within these gates.”
Shirley MacLaine
Shirley MacLaine, who shared the screen with Parton in “Steel Magnolias,” said in a statement to NBC News, “God sent her to us, and she has returned home.”
Kelly Clarkson
Kelly Clarkson reflected on Parton’s legacy and why she was so beloved in her post.

“Dolly Parton had a way of making everyone feel special, and seen, and welcomed, and as if you were old friends,” she explained in her tribute. “I will miss her heart and her voice as I am sure millions will.”
She added, “What an incredible gift and talent she was and still is with an amazing catalogue of art she has left behind for all of us.”
Keith Urban
Keith Urban shared a brief message to his Instagram story that said, “Heartbroken today. Dolly Parton,” and included a broken heart. “Honestly...... I have no words right now.”
Producers of ‘Dolly: A True Original Musical’
The Broadway production inspired by the life and music of Parton said Aug. 25 after her death that the show will still go on.
“As was Dolly’s wish, the Broadway production of DOLLY: A True Original Musical will begin previews December 7 at the St. James Theatre in New York City.”
Keke Palmer
Keke Palmer, who co-starred with Parton in the 2012 musical dramedy “Joyful Noise,” shared a black-and-white photo of the icon on Instagram. She uploaded a picture of them in “Joyful Noise,” as well.
“I’m devastated. Truly,” she said in the caption.
Kacey Musgraves
Kacey Musgraves mourned Parton’s passing in a series of tweets.

“Dolly,” she wrote and included a broken heart emoji. “This one really hurts.” In a follow-up message, Musgraves said, “The world feels a lot less sparkly all of a sudden.” For her final tweet, she added, “So glad she’s with her Carl Dean,” referring to Parton’s late husband who died in 2023. “No one talk to me today.”
Lily Tomlin

Parton’s “9 to 5” co-star Lily Tomlin uploaded Jamie Lee Curtis’ tribute — which said “Thank you, Dolly. For all of it,” beneath a black-and-white snap of Parton and Dean — to her Instagram story. Tomlin added Parton’s version of “I Will Always Love You” to the post.
She then shared a few pictures of Parton on the next slide, including one of them with fellow “9 to 5” star Jane Fonda and their reunion at the 69th Emmy Awards.
She also praised Parton for being a “comedy treasure” in a third slide featuring Parton’s hit “9 to 5.”
Khloé Kardashian
Khloé Kardashian posted a photo to her Instagram story of her with Parton, writing that she was “heartbroken,” along with a longer message about her legacy.

“Some people are so so extraordinary, their existence feels almost impossible. Dolly was one of those people,” she said, in part. “A once-in-a-lifetime soul. A woman whose light, heart, talent and humanity changed this world forever.”
Parton appeared on Kardashian’s podcast, “Khloé In Wonder Land,” last July.
Paris Hilton
Paris Hilton posted a message on X alongside a photo of herself with the country legend.

“Her talent, heart and kindness touched so many lives, and she truly left this world better than she found it,” Hilton wrote. “Sending all my love to her family, friends and everyone who loved her. Rest in peace, Dolly.”
Sarah Jessica Parker
Although she never got the chance to meet her in person, Sarah Jessica Parker still felt a connection to Parton.
In her tribute on Instagram, she wrote, “No!!!!!! I never met @dollyparton but my gosh, did I love her. I don’t think any of us had to know her to love her.”
She called Parton “one of the greatest this country ever produced” and also pointed out her philanthropic efforts.
“What a loss. But aren’t we so lucky,so fortunate for the endless gifts she shared. With the world. Godspeed and RIP. You will be terribly missed,” she said.
Brandi Cyrus

Brandi Cyrus, whose younger sister Miley Cyrus was Parton’s goddaughter, posted three broken hearts on her Instagram story. She also shared a picture of Parton with her horse and added Miley Cyrus’ song “Rainbowland,” which featured Parton.
Grand Ole Opry
The Grand Ole Opry praised Parton for being “a true music icon” in a post on X.

“There is no doubt Dolly’s mark on the world, and on us here at the Grand Ole Opry, will be deeply felt for generations to come. She taught us to always lead with kindness, generosity, and compassion,” the historic music venue said. “May her legacy live on through her songs, the lives she touched, and the countless artists she inspired. There will never, ever be another one like her. We will always love you, Dolly.”
Correction (Aug. 26, 7:55 a.m.): A previous version of this story stated Dolly Parton died at her home in Nashville. The story has been updated to reflect she died at a hospital.

title: Dolly Parton’s Siblings: What to Know About Her 11 Brothers and Sisters
summary: Dolly Parton, who died on Aug. 25, was one of 12 siblings. Her death was announced by her sister Cassie’s son Bryan Seaver. Here’s what to know about Dolly Parton’s siblings.
story: Dolly Parton, country music icon and 10-time Grammy winning singer-songwriter, died “peacefully” on Aug. 25 in Nashville, Tennessee, according to a news release from True Public Relations.
Her death was announced in a video message by her nephew Bryan Seaver, the son of Dolly Parton’s sister Cassie Parton. He did not provide a cause of death.
Dolly Parton is one of 12 children. Raised by Robert and Avie Lee Parton, the kids grew up in the Appalachia region of Tennessee, according to the Country Music Hall of Fame.

Dolly Parton has six living brothers and sisters: Willadeene, Robert Jr., Stella, Cassie, Freida and Rachel. Five of her brothers have died: Larry, in 1955 when he was just a baby; Floyd, in 2018 at age 61; Randy, in 2021 at age 67; David, in 2024 at age 82; and Coy, in July 2026 at age 82, per People.
Read on for everything you need to know about Dolly Parton’s 11 siblings.
Willadeene Parton

Willadeene Parton, born March 24, 1940, is the eldest of Dolly Parton’s siblings. She “tends to act as a second mother to her younger siblings,” according to a post on Dolly Parton’s official website.

Willadeene Parton, now 86, pursued a career as an author. In 1996, she published a memoir about the Parton clan titled “Smoky Mountain Memories: Stories from the Hearts of the Parton Family.” The following year, she released “All-Day Singing & Dinner on the Ground,” a compilation of recipes from the Parton family.
David Parton

David Parton, who worked as a bridge builder superintendent, died Nov. 15, 2024, at age 82 at his home in White Pine, Tennessee, sister Stella Parton announced. A cause of death has not been revealed.
Sharing news of her brother’s death, Stella Parton posted on Threads, saying that her brother “finally got his angel wings. RIP dear soul. Love you forever.”
Before his death, David Parton largely lived his life out of the spotlight, though he had been photographed escorting Dolly Parton to events, according to Woman’s World.
Stella Parton

Stella Parton, an acclaimed musician born May 4, 1949, was 11 when she made her recording debut with sisters Dolly and Cassie Parton, singing on their uncle Bill Owens’ album, per the Smoky Mountain DNA website, which traces Dolly Parton’s family origins.
Since then, Stella Parton has released more than 30 albums, starting with “I Want to Hold You (In My Dreams Tonight),” which came out in 1975.

Stella Parton, now 77, released a memoir in 2011 titled “Tell It Sister, Tell It: Memories, Music and Miracles.” She has explored acting, too, with appearances in the film “Dolly Parton’s Coat of Many Colors” (2015) and “Dolly Parton’s Christmas of Many Colors: Circle of Love” (2016).
While promoting the 2022 Pure Flix original movie “Nothing is Impossible,” Stella Parton revealed to People that she considers herself a “loner in (her) family.”
“Everybody knows that I’m independent,” she said. “But if they need me, if they call me out to help with something, producing, consulting or whatever, I’m always there.”
Cassie Parton
Cassie Parton, born on Feb. 12, 1951, first recorded music at age 10, singing backup vocals with sisters Dolly and Stella Parton, the Smoky Mountain DNA project revealed.
In 1970, she sang with her sisters on “The Porter Wagoner Show,” and she performed as a vocalist in the 2013 Dollywood production “My People: Dolly’s Letter Home,” according to Knox News.
She also appeared in an episode of the TV series “Dolly” and had a role in the 2022 film “Dolly Parton’s Mountain Magic Christmas,” according to IMDb. Nowadays, she leads a fairly private life.
Her son Bryan Seaver served as Dolly Parton’s head of security for two decades.
Randy Parton
Randy Parton, born Dec. 15, 1953, died in 2021 at the age of 67. On Jan. 21, 2021, Dolly shared his death on Facebook, revealing that her brother had died from cancer.

“The family and I are grieving his loss, but we know he is in a better place than we are at this time,” the country icon said in her statement. “We are a family of faith, and we believe that he is with God and that he is joined by members of the family that have gone on before and have welcomed him with joy and open arms.”

Like his older sister, Randy Parton achieved success in music and entertainment. Famous for his headline performances at Dollywood, the singer-songwriter released several hits that graced Billboard’s Hot Country Songs chart, including “Hold Me Like You Never Had Me,” “Shot Full of Love,” “Don’t Cry Baby,” “Oh, No” and “A Stranger in Her Bed,” according to the music publication.
Larry Parton
Larry Parton, Robert and Avie Lee Parton’s ninth child and fifth son, died days after his birth in July 1955. Dolly Parton was 9 years old at the time of her brother’s death.
Floyd Parton
Floyd Parton and twin sister Freida Parton were born June 1, 1957. Like many of his siblings, Floyd Parton pursued a career in the music industry, often collaborating with Dolly Parton.
He penned her 1991 duet with Ricky Van Shelton, “Rockin’ Years” and wrote “Nickels and Dimes” for her 1978 album “Heartbreaker.”
Floyd Parton died Dec. 6, 2018, at the age of 61. The Parton family paid tribute to Floyd Parton at a private memorial in Tennessee, reported Billboard.

“Dolly, and the entire Parton family, wish to thank everyone for their kindness,” the family said in a statement to People at the time. “Yesterday, we laid our sweet baby brother to rest. We all sang his lovely song, ‘Rockin’ Years,’ together as a family at the service to say goodbye to him. He lived a short life of love and beautiful songs.”
Freida Parton
Freida Parton, born June 1, 1957, is Floyd Parton’s twin sister. Freida Parton ventured into the realm of music but diverged from her family’s country origins, singing hard rock songs.

Later in life, Freida Parton became an ordained minister. She told Knoxville News Sentinel in an interview in April 2014 that she had opened Parton Family Wedding Chapel & Antiques, a wedding chapel and store, in the family’s native Sevierville, Tennessee. However, the business appears to have closed.
Rachel Parton George

Rachel Parton George was born on Aug. 31, 1959. She’s known for her portrayal of Doralee Rhodes Brooks in the ABC sitcom “9 to 5,” which was based on the 1980 comedy film of the same name that starred Dolly Parton.

In addition to acting, Rachel Parton George released a country album in 1984, per the Smoky Mountain DNA website. According to her author page for Penguin Random House, she also performed in her family’s singing group.
In September 2024, the youngest sibling of the Parton clan released a cookbook with sister Dolly Parton called “Good Lookin’ Cookin’: A Year of Meals.”
Ahead of the release, Dolly Parton shared a picture of her and her sister on social media.

“The best part of creating this cookbook is getting to spend quality time with my sister Rachel,” Dolly Parton captioned the post with a red heart emoji. “We can’t wait to share our recipes with you all, pre-order now at the link in my bio!”
Coy and Robert Lee Parton Jr.
Dolly’s other siblings — her older brother Coy Parton and younger brother Robert Lee Parton Jr. — largely led lives out of the spotlight.
Coy Parton, who worked as a crane operator, died in July 2026, according to an obituary shared by Atchley Funeral Home. A cause of death was not provided.

title: What Dolly Parton Said About Not Having Children with Husband Carl Dean
summary: Dolly Parton, the country music superstar whose career stretched from the Tennessee mountains to Hollywood, has died.
story: Dolly Parton, the country music superstar whose career stretched from the Tennessee mountains to Hollywood, has died. She was 80.
Her nephew, Bryan Seaver shared the news August 25 on Instagram, remembering Parton’s extraordinary life and legacy. Seaver, whose mother is Parton’s sister Cassie, did not share a cause of death.

Parton’s passing comes more than a year after the loss of her husband, Carl Dean, her partner of nearly six decades, who died at 82 on March 3, 2025, after the pair spent more than 60 years together. The couple did not have children, a subject Parton spoke about candidly over the years, including the way she came to understand that part of her life.
At her request, immediate family will honor Parton at a private service while fans are encouraged to pay tribute to her on social media.
Why Dolly Parton Never Had Children
The couple never had any children, and Parton, 79, has said that her journey to becoming a country music star and successful businesswoman depended on the sacrifices she’s made in her personal life.
Parton spoke with Oprah Winfrey about her career and her life with Dean during an episode of “The Oprah Conversation” on Apple TV+ in 2020.
“Since I had no kids, and my husband was pretty independent, I had freedom,” she said. “So I think a big part of my whole success is the fact that I was free to work.”
Parton also said she was OK with not having children in an interview on TODAY in 2017.
“God has a plan for everything,” she said. “I think it probably was his plan for me not to have kids so everybody’s kids could be mine. And they are now.”

But Parton had been talking about her decision — and her feelings about motherhood — for decades. In a 1984 interview with Interview Magazine, she spoke candidly about never becoming pregnant and how she eventually came to see herself as a mother figure to her extended family.

“I couldn’t have children, I tried to for years. I’ve never been pregnant in my life,” Parton said. “When I was a girl and fooling around, I was scared to death I’d get pregnant, and then when I got married and wanted to have children, I couldn’t have any. But I don’t miss it. I did for awhile, but I realize that I am everybody’s mother. I’ve raised five of my younger brothers and sisters, and now their kids call me Aunt Grannie. I’m like the grandma and the aunt.”
The couple largely lived independent lives while Parton was often off touring and performing, and Dean spent much of his life out of the spotlight after they tied the knot in 1966.
How Dolly Parton Helped Other Children
Parton has been involved in the lives of millions of kids through her Imagination Library, which has gifted hundreds of millions of books to children from birth until they enter kindergarten.

“And I didn’t have children because I believed that God didn’t mean for me to have kids so everybody’s kids could be mine, so I could do things like Imagination Library, because if I hadn’t had the freedom to work, I wouldn’t have done all the things I’ve done,” Parton told Winfrey in 2020. “I wouldn’t be in a position to do all of the things I’m doing now.”

Winfrey also asked Parton if she has had to make sacrifices in order to achieve her level of success, which includes 25 No. 1 songs on the Billboard country charts, 10 Grammy Awards, an acting career and owning the popular theme park Dollywood and several other businesses in her home state of Tennessee.

“I’ve made sacrifices, but I think, like I said, I believe what I know I’m supposed to do,” Parton said. “I’ve made the sacrifice of time ... and not having time to spend with family, and you give up family and friends, vacation, and work without end, 24/7, 365, but you got to make the sacrifice.”

title: Who Was Dolly Parton’s Husband, Carl Dean? Everything She Said About Their 60-Year Marriage
summary: Here’s what Dolly Parton said about her husband Carl Thomas Dean before she died. Here’s a story about their marriage.
story: Dolly Parton and her husband, Carl Thomas Dean, were married for nearly 60 years, and died within a year and a half of each other.
While the country music legend had been in the spotlight since the ‘50s, her relationship with the businessman mostly remained out of the limelight.

Parton, a star on the stage, television and film, died on Aug. 25, 2026, at the age of 80. Her nephew Bryan Seaver confirmed her passing in a video message shared on her Instagram page. He did not mention a cause of death.
The news of her death came about a year after Parton had to postpone multiple concerts as a she faced “health challenges.”
Her death also followed the loss of her beloved husband, who died on March 3, 2025, at the age of 82.
She penned a sweet statement at the time reflecting on their decades of marriage.

“Carl and I spent many wonderful years together. Words can’t do justice to the love we shared for over 60 years. Thank you for your prayers and sympathy,” she wrote on her Instagram, alongside the announcement of his death.
Dean, who was from Nashville, was a businessman without any industry ties. In a 2023 interview for “What Would Dolly Do? Radio,” the singer gave insight into her long-standing private relationship.
“Carl has never been in the limelight and all, never wanted to be in it. He don’t like it,” said Parton.
She shared that after one public outing, he knew that life wasn’t for him.

“He went to one thing with me early on when we first married to a BMI Song of the Year (event), and he came out there taking off his tuxedo, his tie and all that and said, ‘Don’t ever ask me to go to another one of these damn things because I ain’t going,’” she said. “I never asked him and he never did.”
The couple also never had children, though in a 1984 interview with Andy Warhol in Interview Magazine said they tried to “for years.”

Parton spoke about how independence in her marriage led to a thriving career, telling Oprah in 2020, “Since I had no kids, and my husband was pretty independent, I had freedom. I think a big part of my whole success is the fact that I was free to work.
But despite their different approaches to public life, the two had a lasting relationship, celebrating 58 years of marriage before his death.
Here’s a look back at the major events in their relationship, from their first meeting at a laundromat to his support for her music.
Parton and Dean Met in 1964

Many people can live in a city for years before going on a date, but Parton met her husband on her very first day in Nashville. She told the New York Times that she brought a lot of dirty clothes with her, and stopped at the “Wishy-Washy” laundromat.

“After I’d put my clothes in the machine, I started walkin’ down the street, just looking at my new home, and this guy hollered at me, and I waved,” Parton told the New York Times in 1976. “Bein’ from the country, I spoke to everybody. And he came over and, well, it was Carl, my husband.”
In that 1976 interview, Parton had more to say about their first meeting.

“I wouldn’t go out with him. I mean, that was somethin’ we was taught. You gotta know somebody or they may take you on a back road and kill you. But I said, ‘You’re welcome to come up to the house tomorrow because I’m baby‐sittin’ my little nephew.’”
She said he came over every day for a week, and they sat on the porch and talked. “I wouldn’t even take him in the house,” she said.
But the first day she didn’t have to babysit, she said that Dean took her to meet his parents. “Cause he said he knew right the minute he saw me that that’s the one he wanted.”
They Had a Secret 1966 Wedding

After dating for about two years, Dean proposed to her and they wed in May of that same year. While preparing for her wedding, the upcoming nuptials caused tension between her and her then-manager, Fred Foster.
“He asked me not to get married. He said it’ll make it so much harder if you’re married with all this promotion,” she said in a 2012 interview with Chattanooga, Tennessee, NBC affiliate WRCB.
“My mother-in-law had already sent out invitations,” Parton said. “It broke her heart because I said we had to call the wedding off.”

But that didn’t stop the two from getting married in a more private ceremony the following weekend. Only her mother, Avia Lee Owens, and Pastor Don Duvall and his wife were present at Ringgold Baptist Church where they tied the knot.
Parton Wrote ‘Jolene’ in 1973

One of her most famous songs, “Jolene” tells the story of a woman begging for Jolene not to “take her man.” Parton said this was inspired by a “flirtation” that her husband had with a woman working at the local bank.

“She got this terrible crush on my husband,” Parton told NPR in 2008. “And he just loved going to the bank because she paid him so much attention. It was kinda like a running joke between us — when I was saying, ‘Hell, you’re spending a lot of time at the bank. I don’t believe we’ve got that kind of money.’ So it’s really an innocent song all around, but sounds like a dreadful one.”
Parton Got Close with Her Bandleader in the 1980s

In a 1986 interview with Ladies’ Home Journal, republished in her book, “Dolly on Dolly: Interviews and Encounters with Dolly Parton,” the country icon spoke about how she had gotten “wrapped up” in an “affair of the heart” in 1982.

She told the outlet she’d faced the disloyalty of “a special friend, an affair of the heart, which just about killed me. Oh, I cried an ocean. But I ain’t gonna talk about it anymore,” she said, playfully. “I’ve got to keep some mystery.”
Parton said at the time that she and Dean were not divorcing, reiterating what she has said years earlier.

“We’ll just always be together,” she told People in 1982. “To him it’s all a joke. There ain’t a man in this world could ever live up to my husband. That’s one of the things that keeps me from going too far.”

In a 1982 interview with Barbara Walters, Parton confirmed that she’d been stuck at home in Tennessee for health issues alongside her husband. She joked that her months at home had “just about busted” their relationship.
“I’m glad to be going,” she explained. “He’s glad for me to be going and so we’re glad to get back to our abnormal.”
In the Walters interview, Parton added that she and her husband were “flirts” but were faithful “best I know how.”

“I just love people there and ... being a woman away from home, there are these good looking guys that come on to you pretty strong. And every now and then I like to come on pretty strong myself,” she said. “But I know that I’ve got something at home, that I wouldn’t threaten or take a chance on losing for anything in the world.”
Parton Said She and Dean Were Still a Team in 1997

In a 1997 interview with Out Magazine in which she promoted her latest collection of dance club remixes, Parton explained that she and her longtime companion, Judy Ogle, was “just an old maid” and not her lover.

“People think because she’s never married that she must be a lesbian, and because we’ve been together, that we must be lovers. But the fact is, I think Judy would rather be called a lesbian than an old maid,” she quipped. “If I was gay, I’d certainly never find a finer person than Judy as a mate. I’m as close to her just about as I am with (my) husband.”
She also responded to rumors about her husband being out of the picture.
“They don’t ... see my husband because he hates being in the limelight. But I see him all the time,” she told the outlet.
Parton added that the secret to her decadeslong marriage was simple.
“We just make a point to enjoy the stuff we enjoy and stay out of each other’s faces. I don’t get in his s---, and he don’t get in mine. And we get along great.”

The Out interview, along with many others, were reported in the 2017 book “Not Dumb and Not Blonde: Dolly in Conversation.” The book — which cites Parton and Randy Schmidt as authors — collected and published interviews with Parton dating as far back as 1967.
Parton and Dean Renewed Their Vows in 2016
In May 2016, Parton and Dean got the wedding they planned years ago, but never got to have. The private affair was held at their Nashville-area home, and she said they “just had fun with it.”
“I got all dressed up in the most beautiful gown you’ve ever seen and dressed that husband of mine up. He looked like a handsome dude out of Hollywood,” Parton told Rolling Stone.

“We had a few family and friends around. We didn’t plan anything big at all because we didn’t want any kind of strain, any kind of tension, any kind of commotion, so we planned it cleverly and carefully. We just had a simple little ceremony at our chapel at our place. We just had just a few people who needed to be there to make sure they got the pictures and the few things that we needed.”
Parton also said that their vow renewal inspired a large portion of her album “Plain and Simple,” which was released that August.
Parton Surprised Dean with a Playboy Look for His Birthday in 2021
In honor of her husband’s birthday, Parton donned a throwback look that she knew he would love. In July 2021, she put on a Playboy bunny costume in his honor.

“Remember sometime back I said I was going to pose on the cover of Playboy Magazine when I was 75? Well, I’m 75 and they don’t have a magazine anymore,” she said in a video at the time. “But my husband always loved the original cover of ‘Playboy’ so I was trying to think of something to do to make him happy.”

Parton was the first country star to pose for the now-defunct magazine, appearing on the cover in 1978. According to her official website, her contract at the time had “very specific parameters that did not include nudity,” but she still wore the classic bunny suit.
In her 2021 video, she said that she had a new cover made with her fresh outfit and “the new Dolly.”
“Well, the old new Dolly,” she said, good-naturedly. “In the first one, I was kind of a little butterball in that one. Well, I’m string cheese now.”
“But he’ll probably think I’m cream cheese,” Parton said with a wink. “I hope!”
Parton Released Her 2023 Rock Album with Dean’s Support
The singer released her “Rockstar” album in 2023. On “What Would Dolly Do? Radio,” she spoke more about her husband’s reaction to hearing the album.

“I played him the whole album and he said, which to me was the greatest compliment in the world, he said, ‘You know, it’s pretty good,’” she said. “That would be like anybody else saying, ‘Oh, that’s best I ever heard. That’s just so fantastic.’”
She said Dean has always been honest with her about his opinions.

“I had done a couple of things in the past, just some rock things. He said, ‘It’s OK. It’s OK,’” Parton added. “He’s very honest. We have such a great relationship. I know not to ask him if I don’t want an honest answer.”
Parton Announced Dean’s Death in 2025
On March 3, 2025, a statement was shared on Parton’s Instagram announcing the death of her husband.

“Carl Dean, husband of Dolly Parton, passed away March 3rd in Nashville at the age of 82. He will be laid to rest in a private ceremony with immediate family attending. He was survived by his siblings Sandra and Donnie,” the statement read, followed by a personal message by Parton.
“Carl and I spent many wonderful years together. Words can’t do justice to the love we shared for over 60 years,” the singer wrote. “Thank you for your prayers and sympathy.”

title: Jenna and Sheinelle React to Each Other’s Celebrity ‘Hall Passes’ with Surprise and Delight
summary: Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones discuss their celebrity hall passes, which include Colin Firth, Brandi Carlile, Tyson Beckford and Jude Bellingham.
story: Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones have some thoughts about their celebrity hall passes.

For those uninitiated to the concept, the hall pass is the notion that someone in a relationship can explore a romantic or physical relationship with another person without penalty from their significant other.

During the Aug. 25 episode of TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle, the co-hosts agreed a hall pass is nothing more than fun before Jenna said her hall pass “from back in the day” is Academy Award winner Colin Firth.
“He’s very handsome,” Jenna said as a picture of him appeared on the screen.
“That’s your hall pass from days of old?” Sheinelle asked.
“Days of old and days of new,” Jenna replied.
“This is all this is good. I’m getting to know your type,” Sheinelle said.
“I also think it’s a whole vibe. It’s not just aesthetic,” she continued, while Jenna outlined how Firth is British and starred in “Pride and Prejudice” and the “Bridget Jones” movies.
Jenna then mentioned her other choice would be the singer-songwriter Brandi Carlile.
“Also a vibe,” Sheinelle said.
Jenna said Carlile and her wife, Catherine Carlile, are aware that she has previously said she would leave her husband, Henry Hager, for the singer.
“Also, I’ve never kissed a woman,” Jenna told Sheinelle. “I feel like I need to say that. I have a husband, too, so there’s a lot of barriers, but it’s the vibe.”
The conversation then shifted to Sheinelle’s pick. She explained that being on a show like TODAY complicates matters because sometimes she can end up on-air with the person she fancies.
“That’s what happened to me,” she said after recalling how she had a crush on Tyson Beckford.
“The whole world knew I used to be obsessed with Tyson Beckford. I had him in my locker. It was like Tevin Campbell and Tyson Beckford,” she continued as a photo of the model splashed on the screen.
“He’s very handsome,” Jenna said.
Sheinelle said was filling in on TODAY some time ago and co-hosted with Beckford without any issue.

“I have a gear where I like turned off that gear, and then we became and we were cool,” she said before saying they were later seated together at the Victoria’s Secret fashion show, prompting Jenna said she could’ve acted on her crush.
“That’s the thing. It’s different when you have them on your locker versus like, ‘OK, so what’s coming up today?’” Sheinelle said.
Sheinelle then dished on her more current celebrity crush, saying, “I’m more of the auntie in the situation,” while Jenna said it gives off “Lolita vibes.”

“This is cougar vibes, but I’m just saying I think I like a physique, and it happens to be this one,” Sheinelle continued as a picture of British soccer star Jude Bellingham popped up on the screen. “He’s all over my Instagram feed because you can’t lie to Instagram.”
Plus, Sheinelle added, “he seems like a really nice guy.”

title: Country Music Legend Dolly Parton Dies at 80
summary: Dolly Parton, the legendary country music singer who also became a popular star of TV and movies, has died, her family announced.
story: Dolly Parton, the legendary country music singer who also became a popular star of TV and movies, has died, her family announced. She was 80 years old.

Her nephew Bryan Seaver announced her death in a video message shared to Instagram Aug. 25. Seaver, son of Parton’s sister Cassie Parton, did not provide a cause of death. The singer died “peacefully” on Aug. 25 in Nashville, Tennessee, according to a news release from True Public Relations. At her request, immediate family will honor Parton at a private service while fans are encouraged to pay tribute to her on social media.
Weeks before her death, Parton commented on her ongoing health struggles after missing the opening of a new ride at Dollywood.

“I’ve told you before, all my fans, that I’ve had a few little health issues, and sometimes I get a little dizzy and I get dehydrated,” she said in a video that played at the theme park. “So my Nashville doctor has kind of clipped my wings, saying, ‘You ain’t traveling this week.’”
Seaver shared a touching tribute to his aunt in the video announcing her death. He served as her head of security for two decades, following in the footsteps of his father.

“I have imagined the heaviness of this moment, but haven’t truly felt it until now,” Seaver said. “It is an honor, an honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness, but the sadness lies with us, not with Dolly. Dolly has lived in the light, and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by (her late husband) Carl, her parents and countless others who have watched her and longed for her to meet them in the heavens.”
He said Parton “opened doors” for her family as well as “generations of singers, songwriters, musicians and dreamers from every walk of life, and across every continent.”
Parton died a year after her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Thomas Dean, had passed away at age 82. They wed in 1966 and largely kept their relationship out of the spotlight.

Born Dolly Rebecca Parton on Jan. 19, 1946, Parton, the fourth of 12 children, began life in a small log cabin in rural Pittman Center, a rural East Tennessee town near the Great Smoky Mountains. When she was a young girl, her family relocated to a nearby farm in Locust Ridge. Parton’s father, a sharecropper turned tobacco farmer, struggled with illiteracy, which inspired Parton to launch the Imagination Library, a children’s literacy program, in 1995, she told the Belfast Telegraph.
As a child, Parton sang on local television and radio. At 13, Johnny Cash introduced her for her 1959 debut at the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville.

Just a day after graduating high school in 1964, Parton moved to Nashville for a career in music. A multi-instrumentalist, she teamed up with her uncle, Bill Owens, to co-write songs that became hits for Bill Phillips and Skeeter Davis. In 1967, country star and TV personality Porter Wagoner handpicked her to be his new duet partner on “The Porter Wagoner Show.”
In 1967, Parton released her debut solo album, “Hello, I’m Dolly,” which rose to the number 11 spot on the Billboard Top Country Albums chart.

By the early 1970s, Parton had become a solo success. She mined her “dirt poor” upbringing in her homespun lyrics, recalling how her mother compensated for the family’s poverty with her ingenuity on  “Coat of Many Colors,” “My Tennessee Mountain Home,” and scored additional hits with “Travelin Man,” “Jolene” and her own recording of “I Will Always Love You,” which would later become a global hit for Whitney Houston.

Decades before Taylor Swift crossed over from country to pop, Parton, who scored 25 No. 1 singles on the Billboard country music charts, saw her 1977 album “Here You Come Again” landing in the Top 20 on the Billboard pop album chart. The album’s title track becoming Parton’s first Top 10 pop single.
As Parton’s fanbase widened in the mid- to late-1970s, her TV appearances multiplied, including a joint special with Carol Burnett on CBS, “Dolly & Carol in Nashville.”

By the 1980s, Parton had also become a box-office draw. She co-starred with Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin in the hit comedy “9 to 5” (1980), and also wrote and recorded the movie’s chart-topping theme song, earning an Academy Award nomination for best song. Her movie appearances over the years included roles in “The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas” (1982), “Steel Magnolias” (1989) and “Straight Talk” (1992).

Over the decades, Parton’s audience only broadened as she continued releasing music and appearing on television and in movies. She also made frequent in-person appearances at her Dollywood theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee.
Parton gained attention early in her career for her flamboyant onstage attire and bouncy platinum blond wigs.

“My true belief with most things, you’ve got to really find out who you are, what makes you happy, what you’re comfortable in, and if you feel like you look your best, according to your rules, then you are going to do your best. I really believe that,” the singer said on the premiere episode of her 2023 podcast series, “What Would Dolly Do? Radio.”
In recent years, restless Parton showed no signs of slowing down, explaining during a 2023 interview on “Greatest Hits Radio”  that she was not “one to sit around doing nothing.”

“I would never retire. I’ll just hopefully drop dead in the middle of a song on stage someday, and hopefully one I’ve written. That’s how I hope to go,” she said during the chat. “Of course, we don’t have much of a choice in that.”

In 2020, she produced and starred in the Netflix musical film “Dolly Parton’s Christmas on the Square,” for which she won an Emmy. The following year, her 49th solo studio album, “Rockstar,” became her highest-charting Billboard 200 album, peaking in the No. 3 spot. in 2024, Parton announced she was working on an autobiographical Broadway musical scheduled to debut in 2026.
She also made it a point to collaborate with female pop stars decades younger, including Beyoncé, Sabrina Carpenter and goddaughter Miley Cyrus.
Parton and Dean never welcomed children of their own.
“God has a plan for everything,” she said during a visit TODAY in 2017. “I think it probably was his plan for me not to have kids so everybody’s kids could be mine.”
Days before her death, Parton told People that her health issues related to things “I just didn’t pay attention to when I was watching over Carl.”

She first went public about recent “health challenges” in September 2025 after she postponed a string of concerts in Las Vegas. The singer did not specify at the time what health struggles she faced but said, “my doctors tell me that I must have a few procedures.”
In May 2026, Parton said in a video message she was dealing with kidney stones and that her immune system and digestive system “got all out of whack over the past couple of three years.”

“The good news is I’m responding really well to meds and treatments, and I’m improving every day. Now, the bad news is it’s going to take me a little while before I’m up to stage-performance level, because some of the meds and treatments make me a little ‘swimmy-headed,’ as my grandma used to say,” she said at the time.

title: The ‘30 Rock’ Cast Will Reunite for the Show’s 20th Anniversary in a Live Special That Won’t Be Televised
summary: “30 Rock” stars Tina Fey, Alec Baldwin, Tracy Morgan, Jane Krakowski and Jack McBrayer will reunite for a live event in honor of the show’s 20th anniversary.
story: Liz Lemon is back!

“30 Rock” stars Tina Fey, Alec Baldwin, Tracy Morgan, Jane Krakowski and Jack McBrayer will appear at a special one-night only event in honor of the 20th anniversary of the show’s premiere. There will also be appearances by the extended “30 Rock” cast, as well as other special guests.

“Listen up tens, a five is speaking!” Fey said in a press release announcing the event. “Please join us to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the show Tom Shales once said ‘needs a better premise and funnier dialogue … and most of all a more commanding performer in the starring role.’”
All net proceeds from the reunion will benefit The Boys and Girls Club of Harlem.

“We’re honored to be named the charitable partner for this celebration,” Boys and Girls Club of Harlem President and CEO Shaba R. Keys said in the release. “All net proceeds go directly toward the after-school, academic, and career programs that help more than 2,000 Harlem young people each year chart a path to their own futures—and we’re grateful to be part of a night this special.”
When Is the ‘30 Rock’ Event?
The event, which will not be televised, will take place Oct. 11 at New York City’s Radio City Music Hall, which is located across the street from the actual 30 Rockefeller Plaza.
How Can I Get Tickets to the ‘30 Rock’ Event?
Tickets go on sale with various presales beginning Aug. 26 at 10 a.m. ET. The general ticket sale gets underway Aug. 27 at 10 a.m. ET on ticketmaster.com.
“30 Rock,” which was created by Fey, aired for seven seasons between 2006 and 2013 on NBC. The cast previously reunited during the COVID-19 pandemic.

During its run, “30 Rock” won 16 Emmy Awards, including three for outstanding comedy series. Baldwin twice won an Emmy for outstanding actor in a comedy series, while Fey took home outstanding actress in a comedy series once. She also won a pair of Emmys for her writing on the series, as well.
“30 Rock” is currently streaming on Peacock.

title: Why Is Simon Cowell Missing Weeks of ‘America’s Got Talent’?
summary: Simon Cowell’s spot on the “America’s Got Talent” judging panel will be vacant for the next few weeks. Find out why.
story: Simon Cowell’s spot on the “America’s Got Talent” judging panel will be vacant for the next few weeks as he undergoes back surgery.
“Obviously medical matters are private but it’s routine and he will be back in a few weeks,” the 66-year-old music executive’s representative said in a statement to Entertainment Weekly.
Cowell’s rep did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for additional comment.

Cowell sits on the judging panel with Howie Mandel, Sofia Vergara and Mel B. The quartet are currently deciding which contestants will advance from the quarterfinals stage. The rep did not confirm when the toughest judge is expected to return to Season 21, which premiered in June.
It’s not yet confirmed if a guest will fill in for Cowell at the judge’s table.

News of Cowell’s surgery was first reported by TMZ. Sources with direct knowledge told the publication that he is undergoing a routine procedure related to his back and that there is no indication of a new major health crisis.
The television personality has had to undergo an operation to treat his back problems before.

In August 2020, he had a six-hour surgery after breaking his back in multiple places, his rep told TODAY.com at the time. The operation involved many procedures and fusions, and required a metal rod to be placed in Cowell’s back.
A spokesperson said that Cowell injured his back after falling from his electric bike at his home in Malibu.
A year later, he opened up about the severity of the situation while appearing on “The Kelly Clarkson Show.”
“I was like a millimeter away from breaking my spine, which would have been a disaster,” he revealed. “So in a weird way it was kind of meant to happen because I was really pushing my luck.”
Dowel recalled that his son Eric was with him when he was “thrown about 8 feet in the air” and landed on the ground.

“This is at the front of my house and the only thing I thought was, ‘I can’t lie here.’ And you’re not supposed to move. I knew I’d broken my back in that second, somehow managed to get back into my bedroom,” he added.
He said in addition to a large scar, he was left with a titanium rod and screws in his back following the surgery.
Cowell also addressed the accident during an interview with TODAY’s Jason Kennedy in May 2023.
“It was painful, it wasn’t great,” he said about the fall.

“However, I was so unfit before the accident. I didn’t know how unfit I was until I had to do all this stuff afterwards,” he continued. “And I’m like, ‘My God.’ Things like that, I believe, happened for a reason.”
He also shared that he planned to still ride his bike despite the injury.
“I’m obsessed with these things,” he said.

title: ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Reveals Final 3 After Shocking Elimination
summary: Fans are just one episode away from learning which new pro is joining Season 35 this fall. Find out who was eliminated in the semifinals of “DWTS: The Next Pro.”
story: “Dancing With the Stars” fans are just one episode away from learning which new pro is joining Season 35 this fall.

At the end of the latest episode of the summer spinoff series, “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro,” the three finalists were revealed. Judges Mark and Shirley Ballas, as well as guest judge and former pro Kym Johnson, announced the top three after the season’s most shocking elimination.

Episode 7 began with the remaining dancers — Adele Zaikman, AJ Pritchard, Allen Genkin and Selena Hamilton — learning that for the semifinals they would have to choreograph and perform two routines that wowed the judges, just like the pros are asked to do on “DWTS.”
“You’ve all proved you’re great dancers, but now we need to dig deep. To decide whether you have the choreography, the teaching skills and the personality,” Shirley explained.
For their first dance, the contestants were paired with four current pros on the show, creating the following duos:
Adele and Gleb Savchenko dancing the sambaAJ and Rylee Arnold dancing the cha chaAllen and Witney Carson dancing the jiveSerena and Jan Ravnik dancing the salsa
Adele and Gleb Savchenko dancing the samba
AJ and Rylee Arnold dancing the cha cha
Allen and Witney Carson dancing the jive
Serena and Jan Ravnik dancing the salsa
Then, the contestants teamed up with each other for their second dances of the night.
With the best dancers left in the competition, the margin for error was slim. See who impressed the judges enough to earn a spot in the finale.
What Happened During the ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Semifinals?

The first couple to dance was Allen and Witney. Before the performance, Witney mentioned in her feedback during rehearsals that Allen needed to work on his confidence. While he seemed to be the ideal leading man as they danced together, Shirley had some criticisms. She said the two were excellent when they were side by side, but she said Allen’s choreography didn’t highlight enough “wow moments” for Witney. Kym agreed with the critique, although she said the routine included many classic jive moves. Mark disagreed, however, and said it was his favorite jive of the season and he was bouncing in his seat the entire time.

Selena and Jan, who both have backgrounds as commercial dancers, were up next with their steamy salsa. Mark said Selena “nailed the brief” and he could see her routine being performed on “Latin Night” on “DWTS.” Kym called Selena a “star” and applauded her “clever” choreography. Shirley continued to praise her, pointing out Selena’s impressive balance and her chemistry with Jan.

Ahead of taking the dance floor, Adele revealed she was panicking a little and worried she wouldn’t be able to keep up with Gleb. But as soon as the music started, those fears seemed to dissipate. Kym said Adele was a great teacher and that her routine could appear on “DWTS.” Mark compared her fierce dancing to the movements of a “hooded cobra” ready to strike at any moment. Shirley called Adele and Gleb a “power couple,” but reminded Adele that she needs to include more “wow moments” that play to the cameras.

AJ, who has repeatedly shared in past episodes how long he has wanted to be a pro, had an intense rehearsal with Rylee. She expressed concerns about how his teaching style would work with a celebrity on “DWTS.” However, the two earned positive comments from the judges. Shirley said AJ went outside of his comfort zone and showcased Rylee well. Kym said AJ and Rylee’s personalities shined in the dance. But Mark, again, had a slightly different opinion. He said he wanted more “soul and funk and grit” in the routine.
For the second half of the episode, Adele was partnered with AJ for a foxtrot, and Selena and Allen were given the quickstep.

Close friends Allen and Selena danced together first. After the performance, Shirley said “the hardest thing to teach is a personality, and you both shine like bright lights when it comes to that.” Kym said she was most impressed by their creativity and musicality. Mark said the routine had “intention” and he enjoyed how much charisma they exuded.

The final dance of the night was performed by AJ and Adele. Even host Robert Irwin had to compliment the cool routine. Mark said the performance was “gorgeous.” Kym mentioned the chemistry between AJ and Adele and said the dance was “perfection.” Shirley, who constantly gave AJ tough criticism at the start of the competition, called him a “star.” As for Adele, Shirley said she is “the new generation for ‘Dancing With the Stars.’”
Who Was Eliminated on Episode 7, the Semifinals, of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’?
Shirley gave each contestant a compliment before sharing how difficult it was to eliminate one person.
Since there were only four dancers, Shirley opted to just announce the name of the person going home instead of revealing a bottom two.
Shirley said there was one dancer who “ever-so-slightly underperformed.” She announced that Allen had danced for the last time on the show.

Allen said in his last confessional that he was “sad and devastated” to be going home. He added he had a great time and that he hoped he made his late mother proud. Robert told Allen that he connected with Allen’s story and passion. In his final words, Allen said he hoped his time on the show inspired viewers to pursue their dreams.
What Will Happen in the Finale?
Next week, “DWTS: The Next Pro” comes to an end with an epic finale airing on Monday, Aug. 31.

The teaser showed Mark and Shirley dancing together and a live audience joining the ballroom. Plus, each finalist will be paired with three “DWTS” alums: Adam Rippon, Nēv Schulman and Charli D’Amelio.
Who will win and appear on “DWTS” Season 35? Tune in to find out.

title: Tim Curry, star of ‘Rocky Horror Picture Show’ and ‘It,’ dies at 80
summary: The English actor became a fan favorite for his portrayal of Dr. Frank-N-Furter in 1975’s “The Rocky Horror Picture Show,” but he also had a host of other iconic screen performances to his name.
story: Actor Tim Curry, best known for his memorable role as Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the cult classic film “The Rocky Horror Picture Show,” is dead, according to his longtime manager and friend Marcia Hurwitz.
Curry’s representatives said in a statement that he died peacefully at his home in the Toluca Lake neighborhood of Los Angeles on Tuesday.
Los Angeles police said a death investigation report was completed late Tuesday for an 80-year-old man at a home in Los Angeles, though they did not identify the body as Curry’s.
A cause of death has not yet been publicly revealed. He was 80 years old.

While Curry cemented himself as a fan favorite for his portrayal of Dr. Frank-N-Furter in 1975’s “The Rocky Horror Picture Show,” fans of campy horror and mystery films also remember him for his roles as Wadsworth in the movie adaptation of the beloved board game “Clue” and as the evil clown Pennywise in the 1990 TV movie version of Stephen King’s book “It.”
British writer and comedian Jonathan Lynn, who directed “Clue,” told NBC News he last saw Curry about a year ago during an interview.
Lynn, 83, recalled the interviewer’s telling Curry that “he was so well known and yet no one seemed to know him very well. And he said, ‘Well, I think that’s appropriate.’”
The pair had known each other since they were teenagers and even attended the same school in England.
“He told me he had become an actor because I did,” Lynn said.
Add to Google
Add to Google
“Clue” co-stars Lesley Ann Warren, who played Miss Scarlet, and Michael McKean, who played Mr. Green, shared their condolences on social media.

“My dear companion in crime, the brilliant, hilarious, hysterically funny, magician of artistry has left us,” Warren said on Instagram alongside throwback photos of the two together. “What an unbelievable joy to have shared a sound stage with him and to engage with such a master talent.”
McKean said on X that his last conversation with Curry “was about life and love and laughter.”
“Our blessing was that we had Tim Curry in our lives. RIP, my friend,” he wrote.
Curry had long been dealing with health issues following a massive stroke in 2012 that left him partially paralyzed and unable to walk.
Born April 19, 1946, Curry amassed hundreds of credits across film, television and theater throughout a career spanning more than five decades.
He began his career onstage as an actor in the London company of the musical “Hair” before he eventually headed to Los Angeles to focus on his movie and television career.
Younger generations of fans also recognize Curry for playing Rooster Hannigan in the 1982 movie musical “Annie,” acting alongside comedy legend Carol Burnett and Broadway darling Bernadette Peters.
